Louza
22nd April, 1942.

Information from Japanese Advisors of
Shanghai Telephone Company.
....................................................

Sir,

at 5 p.m. 22/4/42 Mr. A.M. McGregor, employee of
the Shanghai Telephone Company visited this Station
and on behalf of the Company requested protection for
the premises at Fokien Road.

Mr. McGregor was sent to the Station at the
request of the Japanese Advisors attached to the
Telephone Company, who have received information that
acts of terrorism, sabotage etc are likely to be more
prevalent in Shanghai and especially Utility Companies
and therefore the Police are requested to take further
precautions with a view to suspecting all persons
entering the Telephone Company, Fokien Road Exchange,
and to have a man patrol round the block.

The Telephone Company have 3 Russian watchman at
the Fokien Road Exchange, one being on duty for 8 hours
at a time, therefore covering day and night. One
Chinese watchman is also employed on the premises, his
duties being to look after the Companies Store Room
and to open and close the gate, leading to the Store.

One C.P.C. is always posted at the Telephone
Company, it will therefore be necessary to have one
more in order to patrol the block.

A/Sen. Det. 1/c.
C. D. I.

D. O. "A" Divn. 24/4

来自上海电话公司日本顾问的情报。
....................................................

先生，

1942年4月22日下午5时，上海电话公司雇员A.M.麦格雷戈（A.M. McGregor）先生造访本警署，代表该公司请求保护其位于福建路的产业。

麦格雷戈先生是应附属于电话公司的日本顾问之要求被派往本警署的，这些顾问收到情报称，恐怖主义、破坏等活动在上海可能更为盛行，尤其是公用事业公司，因此请求警方采取进一步预防措施，以便对所有进入福建路电话交换局的人员保持警惕，并安排一名警员在该街区周围巡逻。

电话公司在福建路交换局雇有3名俄国看守人，每人每次值班8小时，从而覆盖昼夜。该处还雇有一名中国看守人，其职责是看管公司的储藏室，并开关通往储藏室的大门。

一名华捕（C.P.C.）常驻电话公司，因此需要再增派一名华捕以在该街区巡逻。

代理高级侦探 1/c。

SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE.
CONFIDENTIAL REPORT
S.I., Special Branch, SXXXX. File No.................... Date......October 27, 1941.
SUBJECT: Shanghai Telephone Company -
Dismissal of a worker

With reference to the attached confidential
letter obtained from the Shanghai Telephone Company
on the subject of the posting of a notice urging the
workers to contribute money to a recently dismissed
operator No. 1915, enquiries show that this notice
was issued by the "Shanghai Municipality Telephone
Workers' Union", Lane 37, 131 Brenan Road, O.O.L.
The dismissed operator No. 1915 is named Chen
Kao (陳杲), who has been a committee member of
the union. In view of the union's yet small power
among the workers, the union has decided to withhold
any agitation for a strike, but to solicit contributions
from the workers for the benefit of that dismissed
worker. It is confidentially learned that this idea
was promoted by Chao Wei-chung (邵慧忠), operator
No. 1948 attached to the Traffic Office, who is one of
the ringleaders in the formation and operation of the
union.
There is no information to confirm the fears
expressed by a certain operator with regard to Mr. Loh.

D. S. I.
A. C. (Special Branch).

机密报告
特别处情报员，SXXXX。档案号.................... 日期......1941年10月27日。
主题：上海电话公司 -
解雇一名工人

关于从上海电话公司获得的有关张贴通知敦促工人向最近被解雇的1915号接线员捐款的附件机密信件，经查询，该通知由“上海市电话业职工会”发布，地址为老闸捕房辖区布伦安路131号37弄。被解雇的1915号接线员名为陈杲（Chen Kao），他是该工会的委员之一。鉴于工会在工人中的势力尚小，工会决定不进行罢工煽动，而是为该名被解雇工人的利益向工人募集捐款。据密报得知，这一想法是由交通科所属的1948号接线员邵慧忠（Chao Wei-chung）推动的，他是工会组建和运作的头目之一。
没有情报证实某位接线员对罗先生（Mr. Loh）所表达的担忧。

副高级情报员
助理总监（特别处）。

现随函附上供你方参考的一份“通知”及其译文，该通知声称来自工会，内容涉及1915号接线员被解雇一事，昨天早晨发现该通知被钉在卢塞恩分局男接线员休息室的公告板上，并由视察主管移除。*
由于该“通知”是手写的，人们认为它并非由工会发布（工会的通知总是油印的），而可能是由该接线员的一位朋友或由其本人撰写，据说他曾表示，既然工会不帮助他，他就要离开。

page_data.en:
To our Colleagues:

To safeguard our livelihood and to restrict the high handed pressures of
the capitalists, the union has thus been formed to strengthen our unity. But
since the formation on the 4th of May, the Company has been taking all kinds
of possible measures to suppress our movements with one sole intention, to
dissolve the union, that they themselves might have a free hand in the carrying
on of their business.

You should realize that a newly formed union is like a new born child that
needs nursing, and your cooperative effort towards this is desired.

Indication of such oppressive measures has lately become more evident, par-
ticularly in our Traffic Department, for instance, take the case of the dis-
missal of Mr. Chen on the 16th inst. - the reason given was unsatisfactory ser-
vice. We do not deny the possibility that Mr. Chen might have shortcomings, but
the problem is not as simple; for Mr. Chen happens to be one of the most active
members in the union. Therefore we think that his discharge might be due more
to the latter reason than to the former. Your attention is drawn to this and
we know re-occurrence of such cases will follow, though this be the first. Unless
you are willing to demonstrate your power you could easily foretell your own fate.

Irrespective of sex, we should unite for a common fight. Don't look too
much to your own benefit only, for the next mishap might befall on you.

We are not demanding immediate action, but we must express our sympathy for
Mr. Chen, who sacrificed himself for our benefit.

On dismissal, Mr. Chen received only one months salary. Financially he is
exceedingly difficult. We are appealing to you for voluntary assistance. This
monthly contribution is limited to 6 months. Arrangements will be made to collect
on every pay day for 6 consecutive months. Those who are willing to contribute
to this, will please approach Mr. Chow Wen Chung, No.157 Jessfield Lane, Breman
Road. (37 Breman Road).

Union of the Telephone Business
City of Shanghai
page_data.zh:
致我们的同事：

为了保障我们的生计并限制资本家的高压手段，工会由此成立以加强我们的团结。但自5月4日成立以来，公司一直采取各种可能的措施来压制我们的行动，其唯一意图就是解散工会，以便他们自己在经营业务时能够随心所欲。

你们应该意识到，一个新成立的工会就像一个新生儿，需要呵护，因此需要你们为此付出合作努力。

这种压迫措施的迹象最近变得更加明显，特别是在我们的交通科，例如，本月16日陈先生被解雇一案——给出的理由是服务不佳。我们不否认陈先生可能存在缺点的可能性，但问题并不那么简单；因为陈先生碰巧是工会中最活跃的成员之一。因此，我们认为他的被解雇更多是由于后一个原因，而非前一个原因。提请你们注意此事，我们知道此类案件将会再次发生，尽管这是第一起。除非你们愿意展示你们的力量，否则你们可以轻易预见到自己的命运。

不分性别，我们应该团结起来共同斗争。不要只过多地关注自身利益，因为下一次不幸可能会降临到你们头上。

我们并不要求立即采取行动，但我们必须表达对陈先生的同情，他为了我们的利益牺牲了自己。

被解雇时，陈先生仅获得一个月的薪水。他在经济上极其困难。我们呼吁你们提供自愿援助。这项每月捐款限于6个月。将安排在连续6个月的每个发薪日进行收取。愿意为此捐款者，请联系周文忠（Chow Wen Chung）先生，地址为布伦安路杰斯菲尔德弄157号（布伦安路37号）。

上海市电话业工会
上海市

page_data.en:
告同事書

為了要保障我們的生活，為了要減削資方的壓力，
我們才要求組織合理的工會。來單周我們的團結加
強我們的聯絡，可是自從我們的工會在去年五月四日成立
以來，公司方面就是百般阻撓我們的會務的進行，
不但是在暗中或在表面上，資方所用的方法沒有一件
不是很惡毒辣的。資方的一貫政策就是要消滅
我們的組織，解散我們的工會。這是每個同事都洞
悉的。他們要使我們這班手胼足胝的同事失去了
力量的保障，听由他們擺佈，以遂其大人利潤盈囊裏
的願望。

工會自從成立以來，可以說是在驚風浪之中生長
的。當然，新生的工會就似落地的孩子，她之長大成人，培
養的責任全在每一個會員的身上。所以我們希望凡是本
公司的同事，應該負起保姆的任務來培養這可
愛的新生孩子——工會。

近日來公司中的的壓力由暗藏化而轉變至明朗化了。
最易感覺到的就是我們活該的都接連生一切
管理的規則亦益急了：像填諸似的打在我們身上
使我們在工作時失去了一切自由，正式地做一臺機器的附件

益且資方不但就是此滿足而且還在暗中加緊限制我們工
會的活動最明顯的一件事就是十六日陳某同事的被
歇職，這一件事可以說資方向我們進攻的第一炮
以司方面所根據的理由就是不滿意陳某同事的工
作所以必須由王公司繼續工作，當然我們並不隱蔽
陳某同事的短處他在工作方面確有不十分認真之實
可是問題並不如此簡單，因為他在工會中亦是與很
得力的活動分子，他確是工會的熱心办事人。現在
我們撇開陳某同事以前在公司的私人問題而以同事
的立場來講無疑的，陳某同事的解大半是被因
于他是工會中的活動份子，所以我們希望每一個同
事大家起來密切地注意陳某同事這一次的被解
僱的突發事件，因為這是開除同事的第一声，接連
續發生類似的事件正有着呢，假如我們不表出一
些力量來日後我們的命運是可想而知的。
當此大動亂的時期將来临臨的時候我們应与男女
長幼站在一條線上共同奮斗，解除我們的餓深
淵的桎梏，同事們不可顧了自己而拋棄他人須知
这种命運可能隨時加之于每一個人頭上的，祇要看當前

公門中的榜樣，有多少人被打成革籍端開除的不
易。為眼前好過，就苟且的活下去，公門將來對付我
們的手段正多着呢！這一次陳某同事的事件還不
過是開其始端而已！

從陳某同事這一件事情看來，也給了我們全體同事
一個寶貴的教訓，如果我們再是這樣的散漫下去，就
免我們的組織不被消滅殆盡，我們的工會不被解散了
就是每個人的飯碗也要被打翻了。

現在我們查不主張立刻以行動來援助陳某同事，不過
我們對陳某同事之被犧牲應抱無限同情，因為他是一個
為公眾謀福利者。

陳某同事的家庭負擔甚重，現遭此打擊，他決無方
勢難維持，雖在解僱時領到了月薪，但是區區之數何
能接濟他的重累，所以我們想每月各尽所能扶助若干，
但以六個月為限，如果大家肯幫助的話請即向白利南路
兆丰別墅137號鄒文忠處認捐，以後每月底發薪
時派員收取，收至第六個月即行停收。同時我們希望
大家出力來扶植這新生的工會，使他發揚光大！

敬祝
工安

上海市電話業產業工會敬啟

An Operator (member of the Union) today came to the
Service Superintendent and said he had heard from some Union
people that Mr. Loh (Wire Chief in Lucerne) was a spy who
informed the Lucerne Traffic Chief Operator about the Union
activities, and that the Union was going to do something to
Mr. Loh (he thought kidnap him) within the next few days.
page_data.zh: 一名操作员（工会成员）今天来到服务总监处，称他从一些工会人士那里听说，卢塞恩分局的线路主管罗先生（Mr. Loh）是一名间谍，向卢塞恩交通科首席操作员通报工会活动，并且工会将在未来几天内对罗先生采取某种行动（他认为会是绑架）。

page_data.en:
1937 requested an interview...
□□ on sick leave at present - was at the
Veter Hospital this morning when someone came to
his house & left a message for him to attend
a Union Meeting this morning. He states that
he has no sympathy with the Union & has
been forced to join. States that the Union
feel that Mr Roh is a spy & reports Union
actions etc. to Mrs Kagansky or to the No. 1
that the Union are going to do something
to Mr Roh (he thinks laid-off) within the
next few days.
Says that 1948 Clk 70 1965 (dismissed for bad
attendance) 1956 & 1942 are all active
members of the Union. Says he thinks 1942 put
No notice up yesterday. States that 1915 has
now got a job in Nunawading with the Wang
people.
1937 says that he will let me know any
movements of the Union & gave me
his home address in case he was afraid
to come to the Office at any time.

page_data.zh:
1937 [号员工] 请求面谈...
□□ 目前休病假——今天上午有人在维特医院（Veter Hospital）[注：原文如此，疑为Ward或特定医院名] 当他有人来到他家并留口信让他参加今天上午的工会会议时，他正在那里。他表示他对工会没有同情心，是被迫加入的。他说工会认为罗先生（Mr. Roh）[注：此处拼写与上文Loh不同，照录] 是一名间谍，并向卡甘斯基夫人（Mrs Kagansky）或1号人物报告工会行动等。工会将在未来几天内对罗先生采取某种行动（他认为会被解雇）。
他说1948号职员、70号、1965号（因出勤不良被解雇）、1956号和1942号都是工会的活跃成员。他说他认为1942号昨天张贴了通知。他说1915号现在在“王家人”那里的纳纳瓦丁（Nunawading）[注：地名存疑，音译] 找到了一份工作。
1937号说他会让我知道工会的任何动向，并给了我他的家庭住址，以防他任何时候不敢来办公室。
（印：...）

SUBJECT: Shanghai Telephone Company - workers
form union and labour agitation.

On May 4, 1941, a "Shanghai Telephone Trade
Workers' Union" (上海電話業職工會) was formed by workers
of the Shanghai Telephone Company under the auspices of
the Shanghai Branch, Social Movement Direction Committee,
with an office at 44 Tai Feng Ka, Nantao. This
office was recently removed to Lane 37, 131 Brenan
Road, O.O.L. Chun Chien-ming (龔堅民), a member
of the Shanghai Branch, Social Movement Direction
Committee, who is responsible for the labour organization
and agitation in the Shanghai Electric Construction
Company (Shanghai Tramways), is directing the affairs
in the Shanghai Telephone Trade Workers' Union. This
union claims to have 1,000 members among the some 1,600
workers of the Shanghai Telephone Company.

Between 10 a.m. and 12 noon on August 31, some
700 members of the union held a meeting in the auditorium
of the Chinese Chamber of Commerce Building, North
Soochow Road. Apart from holding a memorial service
for the late Woo Chang-foo (胡章富), a worker of the
Shanghai Telephone Company, who died of natural causes,
they passed a resolution that the workers of the Shanghai
Telephone Company unite and further submit the five
old demands for improvement in treatment to the
management of the Shanghai Telephone Company for
consideration.

The leaders of the union are :-
Zao Wei-chung (邵慧忠).

特别处情报员 停滞。档案号.................... 日期 1941年9月4日。

主题：上海电话公司 - 工人
组建工会及劳工煽动。

1941年5月4日，在上海社会运动指导委员会上海分会的主持下，上海电话公司的工人成立了“上海电话业职工会”（上海電話業職工會），办事处设在南市泰丰卡44号。该办事处最近迁至老闸捕房辖区布伦安路131号37弄。龚坚民（Chun Chien-ming），上海社会运动指导委员会上海分会成员，负责上海电气建设公司（上海电车公司）的劳工组织和煽动工作，正在指导上海电话业职工会的事务。该工会声称在上海电话公司约1600名工人中拥有1000名会员。

8月31日上午10时至中午12时之间，约700名工会会员在北苏州路中国商会大楼礼堂举行会议。除了为自然死亡的上海电话公司工人胡章富（Woo Chang-foo）举行追悼会外，他们还通过了一项决议，要求上海电话公司工人团结起来，并进一步向上海电话公司管理层提交五项旧的改善待遇要求以供考虑。

工会领导人为：
邵慧忠（Zao Wei-chung）。

Translation of a letter dated July 19, 1941, addressed to

To
Special Branch,
Shanghai Municipal Police.
July 19, 1941.

Sir,

Owing to the existing high cost of living, we were
compelled to appeal to our management, for amelioration of
our conditions. Some misunderstanding arose, and as a
result certain action was resorted to by a portion of the
workers the other day.

Thanks to the mediation conducted by your Branch, a
settlement of the dispute has been reached.

Keeping in mind that the telephone service constitutes
the nerve centre of this city and further in consideration
of local peace and order, we have been carrying on our
work as usual and have refrained from behaving ourselves
beyond the limits. However, as the basic points of our
demands are still left unattended to, we take the liberty
to make a further request to your branch to bring the matter
to a successful conclusion.

Hereunder are the basic points of our demands for
favour to passing to the management of the Company:-

1. That no workers be dismissed without just cause.
2. That wages be issued during the period of "tai-kung"
strike.
3. That wages be increased according to the following
scale:-

Basic pay             percentage increase
$50 below             40 %
$50 above             20 %
$100 above            10 %

1941年7月19日。

先生，

由于目前生活成本高昂，我们被迫向管理层呼吁改善我们的条件。产生了一些误解，结果前几天部分工人采取了某些行动。

感谢贵处进行的调解，纠纷已达成和解。

考虑到电话服务构成这座城市的神经中枢，并进一步考虑到地方的和平与秩序，我们一直照常开展工作，并克制自己的行为不越出界限。然而，由于我们要求的基本要点仍未得到处理，我们冒昧再次请求贵处促成此事圆满解决。

以下是我们要求的基本要点，恳请转交公司管理层：-

1. 无正当理由不得解雇任何工人。
2. 在“怠工”罢工期间发放工资。
3. 按以下比例增加工资：-

基本工资             增加百分比
50元以下             40 %
50元以上             20 %
100元以上            10 %

1941年7月11日上午11时20分，侦探副督察库克（D.S. Cooke）奉中央捕房高级侦探长希尔（C.D.I. Hill）之命，前往江西路上海电话公司，就该公司华籍雇员中疑似即将发生的劳资纠纷的相关情报，与普林格尔先生（Mr. Pringle）进行了面谈。

据悉，管理层收到情报称，中国电力有限公司（China Electric Co. Ltd）的罢工员工将要对上海电话公司进行“纠察”。但此事并未发生。另获情报称，若上述行动未果，将于今日（1941年7月11日）发动罢工；如果今日未能实现，则下一个可能的日期定为1941年7月14日（星期一）。目前尚不清楚这将是一次总罢工，还是仅限于某个特定部门。

C.D.C.s 144 and 154

Acting on instructions,we proceeded to the vicinity
of the Shanghai Telephone Co.,242 Kiangse Rd. at 9a.m.
11/7/41,on precaution against a strike which might be
precipitated by the said Co.'s workers. At about 11.15a.m.
even date,we observed 2 men appearing like workers.One of
them stated that a strike would be carried out on the 12/7/41
should no settlement be arrived at. Then the other replied
" I cannot help. It is up to the majority." The 1st one
again stated: "It has been heard that if no settlement
is arrived at then they(workers) will blockade the street."
After these conversations,both of them entered the Co. Then
we telephoned to the station,reporting as above. C.D.I.
Fan instructed that this duty be withdrawn at 12m.d. even date.
However,C.D.C.144 was further instructed to visit that vicinity
again at 7a.m. 12/7/41 for further development.

Signed: C.D.S.144,154.
page_data.zh:
刑事侦缉处第144号和154号

奉命行事，我们于1941年7月11日上午9时前往江西路242号上海电话公司附近，以防该公司工人可能引发的罢工。同日约上午11时15分，我们观察到两名看似工人的男子。其中一人表示，若无法达成和解，将于1941年7月12日举行罢工。另一人随即回答：“我无能为力，这取决于大多数人的意见。”第一人再次说道：“听说如果达不成和解，他们（工人）将封锁街道。”谈话结束后，两人进入公司。随后我们打电话向警署报告了上述情况。刑事侦缉长范（C.D.I. Fan）指示于当日中午12时撤除该勤务。然而，刑事侦缉处长第144号又奉命于1941年7月12日上午7时再次前往该地区，以观察进一步事态发展。

签署人：刑事侦缉警士第144号、154号。

Following the formal inaugural meeting of the
Shanghai Municipality Telephone Workers' Union, which
was held on May 4, 1941, in Nantao, identical letters
of a threatening nature were addressed by the union in
the early part of May to a number of senior employees
of the Shanghai Telephone Company including:-

1. Loo Hsiao Tsaung (羅孝章),

Discreet enquiries have shown that in sending these
letters to the senior employees of the Shanghai Telephone
Company, the Shanghai Municipality Telephone Workers' Union

the union but meant to warn the recipients against
retarding the activities of the union.

7th, May 1941.

Dear Mr. Foh Sung,

The cost of everything has gone up extremely high,
rice is now as dear as pearls, and the cost of living has gone to the
highest peak. Really we cannot live, but the Company had never paid
any attention nor had showed any goodwill to its employees, consequently,
it had made the staff of the Telephone Company and the China Electric
Company to cooperate and to fight for our own betterment. We held our
first general meeting on the 4th, instant at Yue Yuan, Nantao, and of
which we expect you must have heard something about. You have been
always enthusiastic towards public welfare work, therefore, we hope
you will do some propaganda work in the Fukien Office and give assistance
to those who are still weak, and at the same time we would like you to
get into the Union as early as possible.

Signed
Representative of the
Labour Union

Whang Foo Sung
Dong.Vang Yue
page_data.zh:
1941年5月7日。

亲爱的福生先生：

万物价格极度上涨，米价贵如珍珠，生活成本已达最高峰。实在难以生存，但公司从未关注也未对员工表示任何善意，因此，这使得电话公司和中国电力公司的员工联合起来，为我们自身的改善而奋斗。我们于本月4日在南市豫园举行了第一次全体大会，对此想必您已有所耳闻。您一直热衷于公益事业，因此，我们希望您在福建路办事处做一些宣传工作，帮助那些仍然软弱的人，同时我们也希望您能尽早加入工会。

签名
工会代表

黄福生
董万月

page_data.en:
Dear sir,

The only way to fight for an opening and to overcome all
difficulties with the present mood of living as well as for the welfare
of the labourers , we must first of all, organize ourselves in the form
of a union. We know you are always enthusiastic towards public acti-
vities, so, no doubt we would like to receive your help and advice in
this case. Therefore, please enroll for a membership immediately, in
order that we may take a lawful step to demand the Company for an in-
crease in salary. We do not have to kill you if dare try to obstruct
with our activities for the ??? will take care of that. Please favour
us with a prompt reply , I am,

The Chief Representative of the Workmen
Lee Ming Seng
page_data.zh:
尊敬的先生：

为了在当前生活状况下争取出路并克服所有困难，同时也为了劳工的福利，我们必须首先以工会的形式组织起来。我们知道您一直热衷于公共活动，因此，毫无疑问，我们希望在此事上得到您的帮助和建议。因此，请立即登记入会，以便我们可以采取合法步骤要求公司加薪。如果您敢阻碍我们的活动，我们不必杀您，因为 ??? 会处理此事。请速予回复，我是，

工人首席代表
李明生

12 An Zen St., Nantao.

The cost of living rises every day. Small wage earners are
suffering terribly. They are therefore forced to join the Union
under the direction of a certain (meaning Japanese) party.
All details appeared on the May 4th issue of local vernaculars.
The aim is to request for better treatment of workers. Although
you hold a very high position and enjoy all the comforts of living
you do not have sympathy for others. This is beastly. But we feel
you will eventually sympathise with us and come to lead us instead
of becoming the under dog of foreigners. Should you show no sympathy
and should the Union fail your sin would be unforgivable. Our thousand
odd members would then rise to kill you. Do not say that we have not
warned you in advance. Please consider carefully.
page_data.zh:
副本
1941年5月9日

南市安仁街12号。

生活成本日益上涨。低薪阶层遭受极大痛苦。因此，他们在某方（意指日本方面）的指导下被迫加入工会。所有详情均见于5月4日的本地中文报刊。其目的是要求更好地对待工人。虽然您身居高位，享受各种舒适生活，但对他人缺乏同情心。这真是兽行。但我们觉得您最终会同情我们，并来领导我们，而不是成为外国人的走狗。如果您不同情，且工会失败，您的罪过将不可饶恕。我们要千余名会员届时将起来杀死您。别说我们没有事先警告您。请慎重考虑。

page_data.en:
May 6th, 1941.

Mr. V.T.Wong,

Due to the incessent increase in the cost of all commodities
and the present high cost of living, people on low wages can hardly
struggle for a living. Now, to find an outlet through this desparate
situation and for our own benefit, we have been compelled to ask for the
aid of the XXX and have organized a Labour Union. Our first general meet-
ing was held on the 4th instant with well over one thousand members pre-
sent. We know you are one of the enthusiasts, and would no doubt be
willing to enroll should you were informed. You are not a traitor nor a
public enemy, therefore, we warn you, for your own safety as well as
for public welfare, to get into the Union as early as possible.

Propaganda Department
Western Area
page_data.zh:
1941年5月6日。

王VT先生：

由于所有商品价格不断上涨以及当前高昂的生活成本，低薪人员几乎难以维持生计。现在，为了摆脱这种绝望的局面并为了我们自身的利益，我们被迫寻求 XXX 的帮助，并组织了一个劳工工会。我们的第一次全体大会于本月4日举行，出席成员超过一千人。我们知道您是热心人士之一，如果得知此事，无疑愿意加入。您不是叛徒也不是公敌，因此，为了您自身的安全以及公共福利，我们警告您尽早加入工会。

宣传部
西区

SUBJECT: Shanghai Municipality Telephone Workers'

The Shanghai Municipality Telephone Workers'
Union (上海市電話工會), situated in the office
of the Shanghai Branch, Social Movement Direction
Committee, 527 Range Road, held an inaugural meeting
at 2 p.m. on May 4, 1941, in the former Nantao Fire
Brigade premises, Yui Yuen (豫園), Nantao. Some
460 persons, all members of the Union and comprising
the following employees, attended the meeting :-

Place of Employment | No. of Workers Attending
---|---
Workers of the Shanghai Telephone Company, 230 Medhurst Road. | 200
Linemen of the China Electric Company, 230 Medhurst Road. | 160
Montigny Exchange of the Shanghai Telephone Company, 106 Rue Palikao and the Pichon Exchange of the Shanghai Telephone Company, 57 Rue Pichon. | 100
 | 460

Tsai Wen Hwei (蔡文煥), an ex-clerk of the
Shanghai Telephone Company at present employed by the
Tairiku Shimpo (大陸新報), a local Japanese daily,
who is the principal promoter of the Shanghai
Municipality Telephone Workers' Union, presided over
the meeting and stated that a set of demands would
be submitted to the Shanghai Telephone Company the
following day, May 5.

With reference to the attached letter from

Prior to the departure from Shanghai to Nanking
of Chang Kuh Chong (張克昌), a responsible member
of the former "Shanghai General Labour Union" at Lane
95, House 10, Edinburgh Road, O.O.L., steps were taken

to organize a "Mutual Aid Society" for the Shanghai
Telephone Company employees. It was then proposed to
collect from the employees of the concern a membership

the management that unrest was in existence amongst

关于附呈的上海电话公司来函，涉及电话员工工会的组建事宜，经查证如下。

在前“上海总工会”负责人张克昌（Chang Kuh Chong）离开上海前往南京之前（该总工会址位于爱丁堡路95弄10号，O.O.L.），他联合以下两名上海电话公司被解雇员工采取了行动，即：

1. 吴宝荣（Woo Pao Yung），上海电话公司领班。

2. 季忠培（Chi Tsung Bei），现为霞飞路丽丽（Li Li）擦鞋店店主，

旨在为上海电话公司员工组织一个“互助社”。当时提议向该公司员工每人收取3美元会费。麦赫斯特路站的全部200名安装苦力加入了该社，1941年1月16日，这些苦力中出现了煽动活动。

福建路站的200名安装苦力中也有一部分加入了该社。然而，据了解，在发起人张克昌从南京返回之前，不会向他们收取会费。

在上一次骚乱中，据称由蔡文焕（Tsai Wen Kwan）负责，苦力们故意让管理层知道存在不安情绪

form, which I am told, is an application for membership in the

headquarters in a building on Range Road which, prior to the
hostilities, was used by the S.N.H.Railway as a hospital.

January 7, 41.

Shanghai Telephone Company - Labour Agitation.

With reference to the attached letter from the Shanghai
Telephone Company enclosing a number of anonymous letters addressed
to the various departments of the firm asking the workers to join
a "Shanghai Telephone Company Employees' Preparatory Committee",
discreet enquiries reveal that the agitation is handled and the
propaganda issued by one Tsai Wen Hwei (    ) , an ex-clerk of
the Facility Department, dismissed about six months ago. Tsai is
now working in the Tairiku Shimpu.

The pamphlet enclosed in the letters is translated as
hereunder:-

"Fellows, get up quickly and join our strong organization.
It is our food and we should take it first! !"

Shanghai Telephone Company
Employees' Preparatory Committee".

Observation among the employees of the firm shows that the
agitation has little effect and the employees are adopting a calm
attitude.

CRIMES AND SPECIAL BRANCHES）

FILED

At 3.p.m. January 21, 1941, on instructions from
A.C. (Special Branch), I interviewed Mr. Streit,
Construction Manager of the Shanghai Telephone Company,
Fokien Road Branch, in connection with labour trouble
involving the Company's construction staff.

Mr. Streit informed me that since 12 noon, January
21, 1941, approximately 90 Chinese employed in the
Construction Department, Medhurst Road have been on
strike following a meeting at 11 a.m. between a
deputation of five of the workers and Mr. Streit.

It is understood that eight men of the Construction
Department have recently been arrested by Central
Station detectives on suspicion of the theft of cable
belonging to the Shanghai Telephone Company (Central
Station Misc. No. 32/41).

The deputation of workers put forward a verbal
request to Mr. Streit that he would ignore any
implications that the eight arrested men might make
against any of the remainder of the Construction
Department employees. The deputation suggested that
the eight arrested men would falsely implicate others
in order to evade questioning by the Central Station
detectives.

Mr. Streit informed the deputation that if they
were innocent of any criminal practices, they had nothing
to fear but should they be implicated in any way, he

Streit 先生告知我，自1941年1月21日中午12时起，麦赫斯特路（Medhurst Road）建筑部雇佣的大约90名华人员工在上午11时五名工人代表与 Streit 先生会面后，一直罢工。

据悉，建筑部八名员工近期因涉嫌盗窃上海电话公司的电缆而被中央捕房侦探逮捕（中央捕房杂项案号 32/41）。

工人代表团向 Streit 先生提出口头请求，希望他不要理会那八名被捕者可能对建筑部其他任何员工做出的牵连指控。代表团暗示，这八名被捕者为了逃避中央捕房侦探的讯问，会虚假地牵连他人。

Streit 先生告知代表团，如果他们是清白的，没有任何犯罪行为，就无需害怕；但如果他们以任何方式被牵连，他

With reference to the labour unrest which

6 - AUG 1939）

Unrest now prevails among the lower grade
Chinese employees of the Shanghai Telephone Company
in the Engineering Plant and Traffic Departments.
They are dissatisfied with the management's recent
concessions made them to cope with the present high
cost of living. According to the new arrangements
effective from June 1, 1939, those employees with pay
of more than $200 are now granted an increase of 20%,
those with pay between $100 and $200 are granted an
increase of 12% in addition to a rice allowance
equivalent to half the price above $11 per picul
(say the price is $20, an allowance of $4.50 is
issued), and those employees with pay less than $100
are granted an increase of 7½% as well as the rice
allowance. The lower grade foreign staff (Russian)
are granted an increase of 20%, while the pay of the
senior foreign staff is increased 65%. Prior to
June 1, the Company granted a flat increase of 7½% and
this increase was cancelled following the new
arrangements. The lower grade Chinese employees
are of the opinion that all the others were granted
an increase, while their rate of increase remains
unaltered.

It is reported that a number of these workers
proposed appealing to the S.M.C. for assistance, and,
if necessary, to the "Shanghai City Government"
authorities, in fighting for an increase in pay.

目前，上海电话公司工程厂和交通部的低级华人员工中存在动荡。他们对管理层最近为应对当前高昂生活成本而给予他们的让步感到不满。根据1939年6月1日生效的新规定，月薪超过 $200 的员工现在获得 20% 的加薪；月薪在 $100 至 $200 之间的员工获得 12% 的加薪，外加米贴，相当于每担（picul）价格超过 $11 部分的一半（例如价格为 $20，则发放 $4.50 的津贴）；月薪低于 $100 的员工获得 7½% 的加薪以及米贴。低级外籍员工（俄籍）获得 20% 的加薪，而高级外籍员工的薪资增加了 65%。在6月1日之前，公司统一给予 7½% 的加薪，随着新规定的实施，这一加薪被取消。低级华人员工认为，其他人都获得了加薪，而他们的加薪幅度保持不变。

据报道，其中一些工人提议向工部局（S.M.C.）寻求帮助，并在必要时向“上海市政府”当局求助，以争取加薪。

Date December 19, 1932.

Subject (in full) Summary of events in connection with the Shanghai Telephone
Company Strike, June 7th, 1932.
Made by D.S.I. Golder Forwarded by Theo Rubenstein, Supt.

A lightening strike of 5 mechanics in the Western
Exchange of the Shanghai Telephone Company commenced at
7 p.m. on June 7, 1932, and was immediately followed by a
strike of the operatives in the six exchanges of the Company
in the International Settlement and the French Concession.
Some little damage was done by the strikers in the Western
Lucerne, Wayside and Boulevard de Montigny Exchanges, but was
of a minor nature and easily repaired. The sudden cessation
of work was due undoubtedly to the gradual dismissal of
operators etc. as the Company turned over to an automatic
system. This change had almost been completed, so that the
Company with the assistance of a few loyal employees were
able to maintain a normal service from 9 p.m. of June 7th,
2 hours after the strike started. On June 10 the Company
estimated that some 1,000 of the 1950 men employed by them
were out on strike. At about 2.15 p.m. on June 9, 1932 some
150 of the strikers congregated outside the Fokien Road
Exchange and sent four of their number in to interview the
manager, they were informed that the head of the firm was
at the head office on Kiangse Road, the crowd were quite
orderly and dispersed at the request of the Police. Later
at the head office on Kiangse Road the four delegates sub-
mitted a letter to the manager, it contained in all fourteen
demands relative to a general rise of wages, the treatment
of the workmen, and the assistance of dismissed workers
whose services were dispensed with as the result of the
change over to the automatic system. The Company promised
that a reply would be given at 10.30 a.m. June 10th.
This the Company would have done, but, owing to the complicated

主题（全称）：关于1932年6月7日上海电话公司罢工事件的摘要。
由特别支部副督察长 Golder 撰写，经 superintendent Theo Rubenstein 转呈。

1932年6月7日晚7时，上海电话公司西区分局的5名机修工发起闪电式罢工，随即该公司位于公共租界及法租界的六个分局的话务员也相继罢工。罢工者在西区卢塞恩（Lucerne）、韦赛德（Wayside）及蒙蒂尼大道（Boulevard de Montigny）分局造成了一些轻微破坏，但性质轻微且易于修复。工作的突然停止无疑是由于公司转向自动系统过程中逐步解雇话务员等员工所致。这一变更已几乎完成，因此在少数忠诚员工的协助下，公司得以在罢工开始两小时后，即6月7日晚9时恢复正常服务。6月10日，公司估计其雇佣的1950名员工中约有1000人参与罢工。1932年6月9日下午约2时15分，约150名罢工者聚集在福建路分局外，并派出四名代表进入分局会见经理，他们被告知公司负责人位于江西路的总公司。人群秩序井然，并在警方的要求下散去。随后，在江西路总公司，这四名代表向经理提交了一封信，信中总共提出了十四项要求，涉及普遍加薪、工人待遇以及对因转为自动系统而被解雇工人的援助问题。公司承诺将于6月10日上午10时30分给予答复。

June 24 with but 40 of the affected men still not returned

C. & S. B. TEL.
3728
5/9/32

TELEPHONE WORKER No.6
August 30.

Editorial Office : Telephone No.55 of the Company.

Slogans : Oppose the dismissal of workers !
Demand the reinstatement of dismissed workers !
Drive away the White Russians !
Organize a Union for the Workers!
Pay a monthly allowance of $12.00 to each of
the unemployed workers !
Double wages to those who work on Sundays and Holidays!
Increase the wages as follows : $10 to those recei-
ving $20 and below; $8 to those receiving $30
or below; $5 to those receiving $40 or below;
$3 to those receiving about $40.

How to Commemorate September 18.

September 18 is the anniversary of Japan's invasion
of the North Eastern Provinces. What we see today is
that the colour of the provinces of China is changing one
after another. The Kuomintang is strictly following a
traitorous and pro-Imperialistic policy. At the same time,
however, 800,000 Volunteers in the North-East are continuing
their brave resistance against the Japanese Imperialists,
while millions of labourers and peasants have raised red
banners and scythes as a sign that they have run away from
Imperialistic and Kuomintang oppression. On the first
anniversary of the September 18 incident, we should therefore
raise funds for the support of the North Eastern Volunteers,
participate in the Dare-to-die Corps to the North, inspect
and confiscate Japanese goods, oppose the partitioning of
China, oppose the attack on Red Armies and participate
in all preparatory meetings to be held to consider ways and
means to commemorate September 18.

Company news.

Central : News has spread widely about the dismissal
of workers by the Telephone Company. Besides dismissing a
large number of workers in the "New Equipment Room", the
capitalists are contemplating discharging the entire body
of workers in the "Ground Line Department".
Northern : The proprietors of the Company are the
cleverest American Imperialists and Capitalists. They are
clever because when they want to dismiss a worker they
first transfer him to another department. This is to avoid
any sympathetic action which may be shown by his fellow
workers. Two men in the Northern "Ground Line Department"
have been transferred and it is said they will be dismissed.
Fokien : The capitalists are dissatisfied with the
workers in the "Automatic Telephone Department" because they
were the leaders in the recent strike. It is learned that
about 40 or 50 of them will be dismissed in August.

Red Army News.

Aug.22, Nanchang : Chu Teh and Pang Teh Wei and their
men have reached Wu-An. The anti-Red forces under Gen. Kao
withdrew without fighting. The Red Army has now captured Nyi
Wang and approaching Nanchang where great alarm has arisen.
Aug.24, Canton : Wen Chong has been captured by Red Army.
ong Kong and Yuin Loh have also been occupied.

1932年9月5日

电话工人第6号
8月30日。

编辑部：公司电话55号。

口号：反对解雇工人！
要求复职被解雇的工人！
驱逐白俄！
组织工人工会！
向每位失业工人每月发放12.00元津贴！
周日及节假日工作者工资加倍！
按以下标准增加工资：月薪20元及以下者增加10元；30元及以下者增加8元；40元及以下者增加5元；约40元者增加3元。

如何纪念九一八。

九月十八日是日本入侵东北各省的周年纪念日。我们今天看到的是，中国各省的色彩正逐一改变。国民党严格奉行卖国和亲帝国主义的政策。然而与此同时，东北的80万义勇军继续英勇抵抗日本帝国主义者，而数百万劳工和农民举起红旗和镰刀，作为他们摆脱帝国主义和国民党压迫的标志。因此，在九一八事变一周年之际，我们应筹集资金支援东北义勇军，参加北上敢死队，检查并没收日货，反对瓜分中国，反对进攻红军，并参与为商讨纪念九一八的方式方法而召开的所有预备会议。

公司动态。

中央局：关于电话公司解雇工人的消息广泛传播。除了在“新设备室”解雇大量工人外，资本家还正考虑解散“地线部”的全体工人。
北部局：公司的老板是最狡猾的美国帝国主义者和资本家。他们的狡猾之处在于，当想要解雇一名工人时，先将其调往另一个部门。这是为了避免其同事可能表现出的同情行动。北部“地线部”已有两人被调动，据说他们将被解雇。
福建局：资本家对“自动电话部”的工人不满，因为他们是最近罢工的领导者。据悉，其中约40或50人将在8月份被解雇。

红军消息。

8月22日，南昌：朱德、彭德怀及其部队已抵达武安。高将军率领的反共部队未战而退。红军现已占领宜黄 (Nyi Wang) 并逼近南昌，引起极大恐慌。
8月24日，广州：温冲 (Wen Chong) 被红军俘虏。香港 (ong Kong) 和云罗 (Yuin Loh) 也被占领。

Aug. 25, Nanking : The red troops in Kompo are now
organizing a permanent "Red" Force and a Soviet Government.

Fourteen Demands :

1. That the present working hours be not increased
and that juvenile workers work only 6 hours per day.
2. That besides increasing the wages according to the
present agreement, increases be given whenever the rental
of houses and prices of commodities go up.
3. Sundays, holidays and days on which the Union holds
meetings should be proclaimed holidays and that
double wages be paid for work on these holidays.
4. That the savings and 6 months' retiring gratuity
be handed for safe custody to the workers themselves.
5. That a sum equivalent to one year's wages be paid to
any worker injured or disabled, that he be allowed to
resume work after having been cured and that a worker
retiring after 50 years of age be issued with a pension.
6. That $5,000.00 be paid to the family of any worker
who dies while discharging his duty.
7. That wages be paid for period of sickness,
marriage or leave, that sick workers be paid medical
expenses and that a Chinese doctor in addition the
present foreign doctor be engaged.
8. That rain coats be issued to outdoor staff, that a monthly
locomotion allowance of $4 be issued to each worker
and that wages for the last month of the year be doubled.
9. That the workers in the Cold Storage Room be treated
the same as ordinary workers, rest during the tiffin time.
10. That the workers in the Boilers' Room be treated in the
same way as the ordinary workers.
11. That Workers be not transferred in their work frequently.
12. That new workers should be employed through the Union.
13. That two months leave be granted to female operators
during child birth with full wages and in addition,
$50 as expenses.
14. That the subscription rates be not increased.

十四项要求：

1. 现有工作时间不得延长，童工每日工作仅限6小时。
2. 除按照现行协议增加工资外，每当房租和物价上涨时，应给予增资。
3. 星期日、节假日以及工会举行会议的日子应宣布为假日，在这些假日工作应支付双倍工资。
4. 储蓄金和6个月的退休酬劳金应交由工人自行保管。
5. 任何受伤或致残的工人应获得相当于一年工资的赔偿，治愈后允许复工，50岁以上退休的工人应发给养老金。
6. 任何在执行职务期间死亡的工人，其家属应获得5,000.00元抚恤金。
7. 病假、婚假或休假期间应支付工资，患病工人应报销医疗费，并在现有外籍医生之外聘请一名中医。
8. 应向户外工作人员发放雨衣，向每位工人每月发放4元交通津贴，年底最后一个月的工资加倍。
9. 冷藏室工人应与普通工人同等对待，午餐时间休息。
10. 锅炉房工人应与普通工人同等对待。
11. 不得频繁调动工人的工作岗位。
12. 新工人应通过工会雇佣。
13. 女接线员分娩期间应给予两个月带薪假期，并额外发放50元费用。
14. 电话费率不得提高。

Translation of a Communist Handbill.
------------------

Young workers of the whole country !
Let us celebrate September 1, International Youth Day,
by strikes, demonstrations and meetings !
Oppose the partition of China by imperialists and the
2nd world war !
Oppose the 4th anti-Red Army expedition launched by
Kuomintang and Imperialists!

September 1 was the date chosen by the young masses and
labourers to oppose the World War. September 1 this year
has been selected by the young masses and labourers to
start their propaganda opposing the partition of China,
the attack on the Soviet Army and the preparation of a
second world war.
The plans for the partition of China and starting of
a second world war have already been started by Japan in
Manchuria and Shanghai. During the fighting in these
places we witnessed innumerable workers being thrown out
of their jobs, killed or injured, rendered homeless or
disabled. The situation is more aggravated by the Kuomintang
attack on the Red Army, their slaughter of the labourers and
peasants, dismissal of workers, increase of work of those
employed, reduction of wages and prohibition of strikes and
meetings.
We must unite together and organize a Committee for
Juvenile Workers. We should also organize the following :
Soviet Friendly Society, Red Army Friendly Society, Anti-
Imperialist Youth Department, and start strikes and
hold meetings, issue manifestoes and circular telegrams
opposing the attack on the Red Army, factory lockouts,
reduction of wages, dismissal of workers etc.
On September 1 this year we should organize Youth Red
Guerilla Corps, which will smash some of the newspaper
offices, other institutions and barracks of the imperialists
and Kuomintang. They will also destroy some of the
military equipments, detain trains or ships which transport
soldiers and ammunition. They will further drive out
those White Russians - strike breakers - from the factories.
On September 1 we should organize Youths' Dare-to-die Corps
and Youths Vanguards which will proceed to the North-East
for the purpose of driving out the Japanese.
Finally the Youth Department of the General Labour Union
asks you to join the Red Army and subdue the imperialists and
Kuomintang militarists.

National General Labour Union.
page_data.zh:
共产主义传单译文。
------------------

全国青年工人们！
让我们通过罢工、示威和集会来庆祝9月1日国际青年节！
反对帝国主义者瓜分中国和第二次世界大战！
反对国民党和帝国主义发动的第四次反红军围剿！

9月1日是青年群众和劳工选定的反对世界大战的日子。今年的9月1日被青年群众和劳工选定为开始宣传反对瓜分中国、进攻苏联军队以及准备第二次世界大战的日子。
日本已经在满洲和上海开始了瓜分中国和发动第二次世界大战的计划。在这些地方的战斗中，我们目睹了无数工人失业、被杀或受伤、无家可归或致残。国民党进攻红军、屠杀劳工和农民、解雇工人、增加在职人员的工作量、降低工资以及禁止罢工和集会，使局势更加恶化。
我们必须团结起来，组织青年工人委员会。我们还应组织以下团体：苏维埃之友社、红军之友社、反帝青年部，并发起罢工、举行会议，发布宣言和通电，反对进攻红军、工厂闭厂、减薪、解雇工人等。
在今年9月1日，我们应组织青年红色游击队，捣毁一些报馆、其他机构和帝国主义及国民党的兵营。他们还将破坏一些军事装备，扣留运送士兵和弹药的火车或轮船。他们还将把那些白俄——罢工破坏者——从工厂中驱逐出去。
在9月1日，我们应组织青年敢死队和青年先锋队，前往东北，目的是驱逐日本人。
最后，总工会青年部呼吁你们加入红军，制服帝国主义者和国民党军阀。

全国总工会。

page_data.en:
SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE
S. B. REGISTRY

THE CHINA FORUM July 2, 1932

Aftermath of Phone
Strike Described;
Savings Abolished

Young Worker Tells Forum of Tactics
Employed to Smash Strike; More
Discharges Due Soon

TRYING TO ORGANIZE

Tactics employed by the Shanghai Telephone Company
and the Yellow Union to smash the recent telephone workers'
strike and the aftermath were described to a representative of
the China Forum this week by a young telephone worker who
was active in the strike leadership.

Since the strike, he reported, the superannuation fund
system, one of the issues of the walkout, has been abolished
by the company altogether. Eighteen of the most active
strike leaders have been discharged. Eighty White Russians
have been taken on and are being broken in on the automatic
machines.

None of the 18 men discharged
have received any portion of the
superannuation funds owing to
them. Twelve of them were paid
their salaries for June 1 to June
7 (the strike began on the last-
named date). The remaining six
haven't even received that much.

Funds Diverted

One of the chief items in the
strikers' demands during the
walkout had to do with the com-
pany's failure to pay workers dis-
charged as a result of the
mechanization program their
legitimate share of the super-
annuation fund. For a worker
who has been with the company
20 years, this would amount to
about $1,000. For a worker with
two to three years service, it
would come to something over
$100.

A worker, for example, earning
$27 a month, would after three
years be entitled to a super-
annuation allowance of $124, or
a percentage of about 6.5 of his
monthly stipend. According to
this worker, not only has this
system now been abolished, but
there appears to be little pro-
spect that workers discharged in
the future (and many such dis-
charges are anticipated) will
receive any portion of the funds
which have been accumulating,
nominally, on their behalf.

More Discharges Due

According to our informant,
more than 1,000 workers will be
discharged within a matter of
some four months as a result of
the completion of the automatic
installations. The company will
then have remaining about 1,000
workers in all for whom, with
the abolition of superannuation
and the non-materialization of
the scheduled wage increase due
in April, coupled to the 34 and
25 percent hikes in the phone
rates, the system of exploitation
will steadily intensify.

Speaking of the way in which
the strike was ended, our in-
formant told of a meeting held
at the Route Pichon exchange on
the night of June 20—the night
before the return of the workers
to their jobs—where the fore-
men, who constitute the sole
"rank and file" of the yellow
union, met with a company
engineer, representatives of the
Bureau of Social Affairs and the
Shanghai Municipal Police from
Central Station.

Lackeys Mobilized

"At this meeting it was
decided that the strike had to
be smashed and the strike com-
mittee broken up. The Yellow
Union foreman took it upon
themselves to mobilize all the
subordinate foremen, about 150
in number, who were ordered to
go to the homes of the workers
and inform them that the de-
mands had been accepted in
principle and that the strike was
over.

"Next morning the Bureau of
Public Safety despatched de-
tectives to the headquarters of
the strike committee where they
threatened the strike leaders
with arrest and imprisonment if
they didn't give up the ship and
call the workers back. The strike
committee told the cops to go
to hell."

Re-organizing Forces

But meanwhile the petty fore-
men, almost always willing
lackeys at times like this, had
done their job too well. This,
combined with the other weak-
nesses and failures outlined in
these columns by L. R. last
week, resulted in a wholesale
return to work on the part of
the workers. The strike com-
mittee never issued any declara-
tion which brought the men back
to their jobs. Not until after the
failure of the strike was a fact
and the movement virtually at
an end under conditions of com-
plete surrender, did the strike
committee reluctantly issue a
statement accepting the end of
the strike as a fait accompli.

The chief problem faced now
by the workers is the solidifying
of their own union. Prior to the
strike they had none. The strike
organization was welded almost
simultaneously with the strike
call. Realizing that serious
dangers lie ahead for them, they
are setting up their own organs
in opposition to the yellow
union, to which only the foremen
belong.

上海公共租界工部局警务处
S. B. 登记处

《中国论坛》1932年7月2日

电话罢工余波详述；
养老金制度被废除

青年工人向《论坛》讲述
用于瓦解罢工的策略；更多
解雇即将发生

试图组织起来

本周，一名在罢工领导层中活跃的青年电话工人向《中国论坛》代表描述了上海电话公司（Shanghai Telephone Company）和黄色工会为瓦解近期电话工人罢工及应对罢工余波所采用的策略。

他报告称，自罢工以来，作为此次停工争议焦点之一的养老金基金制度已被公司彻底废除。18名最积极的罢工领袖已被解雇。公司已录用80名白俄人员，并正在培训他们操作自动交换机。

这18名被解雇的人员中，无人收到任何应得的养老金基金份额。其中12人领取了6月1日至6月7日（罢工始于该日）的薪水。其余6人甚至连这笔钱也未收到。

资金被挪用

罢工期间，罢工者的主要诉求之一涉及公司未能向因机械化计划而被解雇的工人支付其应得的养老金基金份额。对于在公司服务20年的工人而言，这笔金额约为1,000美元。对于服务两至三年的工人，金额则在100美元以上。

例如，一名月薪27美元的工人，在服务三年后有权获得124美元的养老金津贴，约占其月薪的6.5%。据该工人称，不仅该制度现已废除，而且未来被解雇的工人（预计此类解雇将大量发生）似乎也不太可能获得任何名义上为其累积的资金份额。

更多解雇在即

据我们的线人透露，随着自动安装工程的完成，将在约四个月内解雇1,000多名工人。届时，公司将仅剩余约1,000名工人。随着养老金制度的废除、原定4月实施的加薪计划落空，加之电话费率分别上涨34%和25%，剥削体系将 steadily intensify（稳步加剧）。

谈到罢工结束的方式，我们的线人讲述了6月20日晚——即工人复工前夜——在毕勋路（Route Pichon）交换局举行的一次会议。会上，构成黄色工会唯一“基层成员”的领班们，与一名公司工程师、社会局代表以及来自中央捕房（Central Station）的上海公共租界工部局警务处代表进行了会晤。

走狗被动员起来

“在这次会议上，决定必须粉碎罢工并瓦解罢工委员会。黄色工会的领班们主动承担起动员所有下属领班的任务，人数约150人，他们受命前往工人家中，通知工人说诉求已在原则上被接受，罢工已结束。

“次日早晨，公安局派遣侦探前往罢工委员会总部，威胁罢工领袖，如果不放弃抵抗并召回工人，就将逮捕并监禁他们。罢工委员会让警察滚蛋。”

重组力量

但与此同时，那些在此类时刻几乎总是甘愿充当走狗的 petty foremen（小领班/副领班）把活儿干得太过头了。这一点，加上L. R.上周在本栏指出的其他弱点和失败，导致工人大规模复工。罢工委员会从未发布任何号召工人复工的声明。直到罢工失败成为事实，运动在完全投降的条件下实际上已结束时，罢工委员会才不情愿地发表声明，接受罢工结束这一既成事实。

工人们现在面临的主要问题是巩固他们自己的工会。罢工前他们没有任何工会。罢工组织几乎是与罢工号召同时建立的。意识到前方存在严重危险，他们正在建立自己的机构，以对抗只有领班才加入的黄色工会。

June 25, 1932

THE CHINA FORUM

Internal Weakness
Helps Smash Phone
Workers’ Walkout

Failure of Pickets, Inadequacy of Strike
Propaganda, Sabotage Within Ranks
Contribute to Surrender

BY L. R.

After fifteen days of courageous struggle, the strike of the Shanghai telephone workers came to an end on June 22 in complete defeat and unconditional surrender. The usual combination of internal weaknesses and outside pressure, recurrent wherever workers are not adequately organized in their own interest, lay behind the failure of the strike action. A worker who was actively engaged in the strike discussed its failure with the China Forum in an interview shortly after the greater number of the workers had returned to their jobs. He listed five basic causes for the defeat.
1. Inadequate and poorly organized picketing.
2. Too great a gap between the strike committee and the mass of the strikers.
3. The failure of the strike to paralyse the telephone service.
4. Insufficient public support caused by inadequate propaganda.
5. The betrayals and sabotage of yellow unionists and traitors in the ranks.

“Yet we are not entirely defeated,” he declared. “We have learned much from our strike. It was called by ourselves and we ran it ourselves. The mistakes were ours and we shall not make them a second time. We have gone back to our jobs, but only the foremen and the traitors have gone back willingly. We are preparing to strike another blow. We are forging our irons in the fire of struggle. This strike helped weld those irons. Therefore it cannot really be said that we gained nothing, even though it failed in all of its demands.”

Ineffective Organization

The strike committee, he pointed out, passed a resolution for the formation of branch organizations which would have carried through the task of organizing the picketing. But this resolution was never put into effect. As a result the committee never really knew how many pickets were at hand and what they were doing. Consequently enough workers remained on the job to keep the service going.

“The strike committee kept too close to its hotel,” said our informant. “Although it was honestly working in the interests of the workers—at any rate after we reorganized it—its resolutions were not actively carried down through the ranks of the workers. Unless we went to the hotel for news, we had to depend on the newspapers to see what progress we were making.”

Gap Used By Traitors

This gap between the committee and the mass of the strikers was put to good advantage by traitors in the ranks, who spread malicious rumors, telling one section of the workers that another had gone back to work, etc. They tried to demoralize the strikers by shaking their confidence in the committee.

In the meetings that were held they deliberately made trouble on small points to keep the gathering from concentrating on the central issues involved. They even led groups of the workers back to their jobs. When the workers themselves, as we reported last week, threw out three members of the strike committee and reorganized it, the men who were discharged from their posts on the committee, Ung Chen hwa, Chen Tse-yun and a man named Pan, immediately set up an opposition strike committee and tried to pose more conciliatory demands. They drew in weaker sections of the workers behind them and gave rise to the reports of a “split” in the ranks of the strikers.

Service Unaffected

The automatic telephone machines, with girl operators still on the job, continued to function throughout the period of the strike. “This was of course a fundamental cause of our defeat,” said our worker friend. “The company could talk turkey

1932年6月25日

《中国论坛》

内部弱点助长
电话工人罢工
被瓦解

纠察队失败、罢工宣传不足、
队伍内部的破坏活动导致投降

作者：L. R.

经过十五天的英勇斗争，上海电话工人的罢工于6月22日以彻底失败和无条件投降告终。内部弱点与外部压力的通常结合——在工人未能充分组织起来维护自身利益的地方屡见不鲜——是这次罢工行动失败的背后原因。一名积极参与罢工的工人在大多数工人复工后不久接受《中国论坛》采访时讨论了罢工的失败。他列举了导致失败的五个基本原因。
1. 纠察队组织不力且安排不当。
2. 罢工委员会与广大罢工群众之间存在巨大隔阂。
3. 罢工未能使电话服务瘫痪。
4. 由于宣传不足，缺乏足够的公众支持。
5. 黄色工会分子和队伍内部叛徒的背叛与破坏活动。

“然而我们并未完全失败，”他宣称。“我们从罢工中学到了很多。罢工是由我们自己发起并由我们自己运作的。错误是我们犯的，我们不会再犯第二次。我们回到了工作岗位，但只有领班和叛徒是自愿回去的。我们正准备再次出击。我们在斗争的烈火中锻造我们的铁器。这次罢工有助于锻造这些铁器。因此，尽管我们在所有诉求上都失败了，但不能说我们一无所获。”

组织无效

他指出，罢工委员会通过了一项决议，要求成立分支机构，以执行组织纠察队的任务。但这项决议从未付诸实施。结果，委员会始终不清楚手头有多少纠察队员以及他们在做什么。因此，有足够的工人留在岗位上维持服务运行。

“罢工委员会离他们的旅馆太近了，”我们的线人说。“虽然它确实在为工人利益工作——至少在我们改组之后是这样——但其决议并未积极贯彻到工人队伍中。除非我们去旅馆获取消息，否则我们就得依靠报纸来了解进展。”

叛徒利用隔阂

委员会与广大罢工群众之间的这种隔阂被队伍内部的叛徒充分利用，他们散布恶意谣言，告诉一部分工人另一部分人已经复工等等。他们试图通过动摇工人对委员会的信心来瓦解罢工者的士气。

在举行的会议上，他们故意在小问题上制造麻烦，使集会无法集中关注所涉及的核心问题。他们甚至带领部分工人回到工作岗位。正如我们上周报道的那样，当工人自己罢免了三名罢工委员会成员并对其进行改组时，被免去委员会职务的翁振华（Ung Chen hwa，音译）、陈子云（Chen Tse-yun，音译）和一名姓潘的男子立即成立了一个反对派罢工委员会，并试图提出更具调和性的诉求。他们拉拢了工人中较软弱的阶层跟随他们，并引发了关于罢工队伍“分裂”的报道。

服务未受影响

在女接线员仍在岗的情况下，自动电话机在整个罢工期间继续运转。“这当然是我们失败的根本原因，”我们的工人朋友说。“公司可以谈正事
（续第3页）

SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL COUNCIL
C. & S. B. REGISTRY
20 June 1932
No. D 3428
Date 23 / 6 / 32

TO THE WORKERS OF SHANGHAI TELEPHONE COMPANY
This Statement is in reply to the Questions of some Workers

1. DISMISSALS: There have been and there will be no unreasonable dismissals. But nothing that the Company can do or promise can prevent the necessity for a reduction in the force - and this reduction is not yet complete. There are 3 reasons for this necessity.

(1) A large number of persons were taken on for the purpose of Construction and for other temporary work in connection with the Conversion Programme.

(2) The reconstructed system requires less persons to work it than the old system.

(3) Financial stringency requires the Company to make every possible effort to reduce expense.

Its duty as a Public Utility forces the Company to do its best to administer its system with efficiency.

Provident Fund: Any person in good standing paid off for lack of work will receive the amount standing in his name in the Provident Fund - none of this money has been contributed by the workers. It must be noted that temporary workers are not in this Fund and that others do not come into it until they have had two years service. Also that refusal to carry out duties disqualifies any person from all benefits.

Wages: Any person in good standing, paid off for lack of work, will receive one month's pay in addition to the wages due to him up to the day on which he ceases to work.

2. APRIL INCREASE OF WAGES: There can not be any promise of automatic annual increase of wages. Increase must always have regard to merit and to the financial condition of the Company.

3. PAY DURING STRIKE: The Company has already announced that there can be no pay during the strike period. There can be no difference between those who strike willingly and those who are unwilling strikers.

4. PAY ON SUNDAYS AND HOLIDAYS: As a Public Utility the Company's system must be at work always, night, day or holidays; duties which require the normal number of hours of work are not paid for at overtime

1932年6月20日
编号 D 3428
日期 32年6月23日

致上海电话公司工人
本声明系答复部分工人的提问

1. 解雇：过去没有，将来也不会有不合理的解雇。但无论公司采取何种措施或作出何种承诺，都无法避免裁减人员的必要性——且这一裁减工作尚未完成。造成这种必要性的原因有三：

(1) 为配合转换计划（Conversion Programme），公司雇佣了大量人员从事建设及其他临时性工作。

(2) 重组后的系统所需操作人员少于旧系统。

(3) 财政紧缩要求公司尽一切可能削减开支。

作为公用事业机构，公司的职责要求其必须尽力高效管理系统。

公积金：任何因缺乏工作而被解雇且信誉良好的员工，将获得其名下公积金账户中的金额——这笔钱并非由工人缴纳。必须指出，临时工不在此基金范围内，其他员工也需在服务满两年后方可加入。此外，拒绝履行职责将导致任何人丧失所有福利资格。

工资：任何因缺乏工作而被解雇且信誉良好的员工，除获得截至停止工作当日应付的工资外，还将额外获得一个月的工资。

2. 四月加薪：公司无法承诺每年自动加薪。加薪必须始终考虑到员工的功绩以及公司的财务状况。

3. 罢工期间工资：公司已宣布，罢工期间不发工资。自愿罢工者与非自愿罢工者之间没有任何区别。

4. 周日及节假日工资：作为公用事业机构，公司的系统必须全天候运行，无论是夜间、白天还是节假日；属于正常工作小时数范围内的职责不按加班费率支付，但对于额外的工作时间，仍按以往的常规加班费率支付。

page_data.en:

rates, but for additional hours of work, regular overtime
rates apply as before.

5.CHANGE IN SICK & OTHER LEAVE: The Company is not aware of the
necessity for any change, but is of course willing to examine any request
for change, if made after return to work and through the usual channels
of Company Organization.

6. YEARLY BONUS: No plan exists for change in the yearly bonus. It
was given in February of this year. This question also is dependent upon
the financial condition of the Company.

7. DEATH OR INJURY: The answer is the same as in No.5.

From these questions and from statements by the Strike Committee, the
belief of the Company is confirmed that the Workers are being misled by
mischievous persons. The following is a list of some of the untruths
which have been circulated to the Workers.

UNTRUTHS

Answer
1.Extra work was performed during hostilities
but the Company did not issue extra pay. Untrue.

2.The Company only issued free food to workers
in North Exchange. Untrue.

3.Ten cents per family per day for temporary
housing is a lucrative proposition for the Company. Untrue.

4.The Company is working at a profit. Untrue.

5.The Provident Fund has been confiscated. Untrue.

6.Contributions to Provident Fund are deducted
from the Wages of employees. Untrue.

7.The Company has employed several hundred
White Russians in the place of Chinese. Untrue.

8.The Company is planning to employ Russians
in the place of Chinese. Untrue.

9.Damage was not done to the automatic equipment. Untrue.

10. 3,000 persons, the whole body of workers have
walked out. Untrue.

5. 病假及其他假期的变更：公司认为没有必要进行任何变更，但如果工人在复工后通过公司组织的正常渠道提出变更请求，公司当然愿意予以审查。

6. 年终奖金：目前没有改变年终奖金的计划。今年二月已发放了年终奖金。这一问题同样取决于公司的财务状况。

7. 死亡或受伤：答复同第5条。

从这些问题以及罢工委员会的声明中，公司确信工人正受到别有用心者的误导。以下是向工人散布的一些不实之辞及其答复。

不实之辞

答复
1. 在敌对行动期间进行了额外工作，但公司未发放额外工资。不实。

2. 公司仅向北交换局（North Exchange）的工人提供免费食物。不实。

3. 每个家庭每天十美分的临时住房费用对公司来说是一项有利可图的业务。不实。

4. 公司正在盈利。不实。

5. 公积金已被没收。不实。

6. 公积金缴款是从雇员工资中扣除的。不实。

7. 公司雇佣了数百名白俄取代中国人。不实。

8. 公司正计划雇佣俄国人取代中国人。不实。

9. 自动设备未受损坏。不实。

10. 3,000人，即全体工人，都已罢工离岗。不实。

page_data.en:
-3-

11. The Strike Committee represents
the wishes of the whole body of workers.    Untrue.

12. The 3,000 Chinese Workers and members
of the Staff have shown their unanimous will
to strike.                                  Untrue.

It is also clear that untruths are being told to the effect that
the worker is being exploited by the capitalist. The fact is that the
worker is getting a fair deal, and the persons who supply the capital
are getting either a very poor reward or none at all.

Service in the Company is not hardship; it is comparable with
that of other Utilities. The wages are reasonable and are paid when
due. The hours are not excessive and the chances of promotion in a
growing company are reasonable.

SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE
C. & S. B. REGISTRY
No. D 7728
Date 21 / 6 / 32

Labour (3)

Shanghai Telephone Company - Strike Situation

The strike situation remains unchanged despite attempts
by pickets this morning, June 20, to intimidate workers entering
the Settlement from Chapei by way of Markham Road Bridge.
Information was received by the Municipal Police on June 19
that the so-called Strike Committee planned to intensify the
movement with effect from this morning by picketing, with
special attention to strikers who have resumed work. The
Communication Office of the Strikers continues to shift from
one lodging house to another in an attempt to shake off police
observation.

The following two cases of telephone cables being cut
were reported to the police on June 18 :-

On the morning of June 18 it was found that a telephone
terminal had been removed and a cable cut in Ting Foong Li,
Hankow Road, thereby disconnecting 18 lines.

The same morning a cable located in Dau Ts Li, Foochow Road,
was found to be cut, 16 lines being disconnected.

The following kinds of handbills were found on June 19
in Room 186 Yia Chow Hotel, following its vacation as a
communication office of the Strikers :-

1. Leaflet entitled "Telephone Company Strike Express" dated
June 16 purporting to emanate from the Strike Committee.
Apart from denouncing the capitalists for adopting suppressive
measures, as well as the so-called treacherous labourers, it
claims that support has been offered by people in various
walks of life.

2. Handbill entitled "Reason for assisting the North Eastern
Volunteer Armies and Strikers of the Shanghai Telephone
Company, purporting to emanate from the Federation of Shanghai
People to Oppose the Agreement to cease Hostilities and to
Support the North Eastern Volunteer Armies of which the
following is a translation :
page_data.zh:

劳工 (3)

上海电话公司 - 罢工局势

尽管纠察队于今晨（6月20日）试图在马克姆路大桥（Markham Road Bridge）恐吓经此从闸北进入租界的工人，但罢工局势保持不变。公共租界警务处于6月19日收到情报称，所谓的罢工委员会计划从今天早晨起通过纠察行动加剧运动，特别关注那些已复工的罢工者。罢工者的联络处继续从一个旅馆转移到另一个旅馆，试图摆脱警方的监视。

以下两起电话电缆被切断的案件于6月18日报警：

6月18日上午，发现汉口路鼎丰里（Ting Foong Li）的一个电话终端被拆除，一根电缆被切断，导致18条线路中断。

同日上午，发现福州路道止里（Dau Ts Li）的一根电缆被切断，导致16条线路中断。

6月19日，在亚周酒店（Yia Chow Hotel）186室发现了以下几种传单，该房间此前曾作为罢工者的联络处：

1. 题为《电话公司罢工快报》的传单，日期为6月16日，声称出自罢工委员会。除了谴责资本家采取镇压措施以及所谓的奸诈劳工外，还声称得到了各界人士的支持。

2. 题为《援助东北义勇军及上海电话公司罢工者理由》的传单，声称出自“上海市民反对停战协定支援东北义勇军联合会”，译文如下：

page_data.en:
Labour (4)

"The North Eastern Volunteer Armies are fighting with the
"utmost bravery under extremely trying circumstances. They
"fight to oppose and overthrow Japanese Imperialism, as well
"as to recover China's lost territory. The strike declared
"by the Shanghai Telephone workers is also to oppose Imperialism
"and to struggle for Chinese emanacipation. Their idea is
"equally great and their action is glorious.
"At present the intrigue practised by all the imperialists
"in order to partition China has been gradually made public
"by the "September 18th" Incident, the proposals to hold a
"round table conference, to establish a "Shanghai Free City"
"and to publicly control the North East. If we wish to
"avoid becoming slaves of the Imperialists, we must show a
"united front and fight with all our might. We should not
"look with folded arms upon the anti-Japanese and anti-
"Imperialism movements. The North Eastern Volunteer Armies
"are in need of our support in order that they may gain a
"final victory. On these grounds, we organized the special
"contribution soliciting groups to solicit from the public,
"funds for the support of the Volunteer Armies and the strikers
"in question. We hope the public will contribute as much as
"possible in order to save us from slavery."

The following is translation of a third manifesto issued
by the Shanghai Telephone Company Strike Committee:

"We, 3,000 labour comrades, have been on strike for the past
ten days to safeguard our own welfare, resist the attack from the
Imperialists and oppose the proposal to increase the telephone
charges.
"In these ten days, the Capitalists have employed all sorts
of methods to dissipate our strength such as the utilization of
police to arrest our representative, the 'buying over' of labour
traitors and foremen to counteract the activities of our Strike
Committee, the deceitful means to persuade some of our comrades
to resume work and at the same time they allege that the strike
was simply due to the agitation of a few mischievous individuals.
Now the Company appears to be in a state of panic as a result
of our persistent efforts in our strike but nevertheless it is
still trying to maintain its power and might. We have
clearly perceived the situation of the Company and the
oppression we have received can no longer be endured. The
only way is to prolong our strike should the Company leave our
demands unanswered. We believe that we will gain the final
victory.
"Although the running dogs of the Imperialists were
driven out by our labour comrades yet they are still actively
engaged in an attempt to dissipate our strength by such means
as the establishment of an office in a certain hotel for
the purpose of destroying our strike union and cheating our
comrades into resuming work by false negotiations.
page_data.zh:
劳工 (4)

“东北义勇军在极其艰难的环境下英勇作战。他们战斗是为了反对和推翻日本帝国主义，并收复中国失地。上海电话工人宣布的罢工也是为了反对帝国主义，争取中国解放。他们的思想同样伟大，行动光荣。
目前，所有帝国主义者为瓜分中国而实施的阴谋，已通过‘九一八’事变、召开圆桌会议的建议、建立‘上海自由市’以及公开控制东北等行径逐渐公之于众。如果我们希望避免成为帝国主义的奴隶，就必须展示统一战线，全力奋战。我们不应袖手旁观反日和反帝国主义运动。东北义勇军需要我们的支持，以取得最终胜利。基于此，我们组织了特别募捐小组，向公众募集资金支持义勇军及相关罢工者。我们希望公众尽可能捐款，以使我们免于沦为奴隶。”

以下是上海电话公司罢工委员会发布的第三份宣言的译文：

“我们三千名劳工同志，为保障自身福利、抵抗帝国主义攻击并反对增加电话费的提议，已罢工十天。
在这十天里，资本家 employing 各种手段来瓦解我们的力量，如利用警察逮捕我们的代表，‘收买’劳工叛徒和工头以对抗我们罢工委员会的活动，用欺骗手段劝诱部分同志复工，同时声称罢工仅仅是由于少数别有用心者的煽动。现在，由于我们坚持罢工，公司似乎陷入恐慌，但仍试图维持其权势。我们已清楚地看清了公司的处境，我们所受的压迫已无法忍受。如果公司对我们的要求不予回应，唯一的办法就是延长罢工。我们相信我们将取得最终胜利。
虽然帝国主义的走狗已被我们的劳工同志赶走，但他们仍积极活动，试图通过在某酒店设立办事处等手段来瓦解我们的罢工工会，并通过虚假谈判欺骗我们的同志复工。

page_data.en:
Labour (5) June 20, 1925.

"It is obvious that the only means which these running
dogs can employ is the instigation of our comrades to
disobey the will of the Strike Committee hoping that we
will all resume work and at the same time negotiate with
the Company personally. In one instance the foreman Yao
Ngo-sung (姚吳松) cheated the workers of the New Equipment
Department into resuming work by deceiving them that the
Company had made concessions. The result in this case
was that the workers immediately left the Company when the
true story was known and also the foreman Yao Ngo-sung
was severely beaten. This shows that the entire body
of workers are fighting for their demands. Work will
not be resumed unless the demands are answered satisfactorily.
By the ten days' experience we have learned that only by
unified action and by obedience to the order of the Strike
Committee can we resist the Capitalists and the Imperialists
and gain the final victory. This is the only way to
protect ourselves from the attack of the labour traitors
and running dogs. At the same time, whenever any such
traitors or running dogs are discovered, they should be
dealt with direct at the Court of the Strike Committee.
"We have already requested all workers of this district
to adopt unified action in enforcing their own demands.
We also requested the French and Chinese Electricity com-
panies, the Chung Hwa Book Store and various cotton mills,
tobacco factories and schools to send representatives
immediately to our Strike Committee to discuss the adoption
of unified steps which are indispensable in fighting
against the Imperialistic capitalists so that the final
victory may be more easily gained.
We request the citizens of this District, various
bodies, telephone subscribers and the newspapers to support
us in fighting the Imperialistic capitalists. We earnestly
hope that they will give us financial support in order to
enable us to prolong our strike until we obtain successful
conclusion to our demands. We heartily welcome any
organization which will raise strike funds for us and also
those who encourage us in our fight. We strongly oppose
those who intend to dissipate our strength as well as those
who are attempting to mediate in the dispute, as only
workers and capitalists are concerned in the negotiation
and therefore any interference by a third party is un-
warranted and will be strongly opposed."

劳工 (5) 1925年6月20日。*注：原文年份疑似OCR错误或笔误，结合上下文应为1932年*

“显然，这些走狗能使用的唯一手段就是煽动我们的同志违背罢工委员会的意志，希望我们都复工，并同时与公司个人进行谈判。有一个案例是，工头姚吴松（Yao Ngo-sung）欺骗新设备部的工人，谎称公司已做出让步，诱使他们复工。结果是，当真相大白时，工人们立即离开了公司，工头姚吴松也被痛打。这表明全体工人都在为他们的要求而战。除非要求得到满意答复，否则不会复工。通过十天的经验，我们认识到，只有统一行动并服从罢工委员会的命令，才能抵抗资本家和帝国主义，取得最终胜利。这是保护我们自己免受劳工叛徒和走狗攻击的唯一途径。同时，一旦发现此类叛徒或走狗，应直接在罢工委员会法庭上予以处置。
我们已请求本地区所有工人采取统一行动，强制执行他们的要求。我们还请求法商和华商电气公司、中华书局以及各棉纺厂、烟草厂和学校立即派代表到我们的罢工委员会，讨论采取统一步骤，这对于对抗帝国主义资本家至关重要，以便更容易取得最终胜利。
我们请求本地区市民、各团体、电话用户和报纸支持我们对抗帝国主义资本家。我们恳切希望他们给予我们财政支持，使我们能够延长罢工，直到我们的要求得到圆满解决。我们热烈欢迎任何为我们筹集罢工基金的组织，以及鼓励我们斗争的人士。我们强烈反对那些意图瓦解我们力量的人，以及试图调解纠纷的人，因为只有工人和资本家才涉及谈判，因此任何第三方的干涉都是无正当理由的，并将遭到强烈反对。”

West Hongkew Station,
Date 20th June 19 32

Subject (in full) Re abduction of Shanghai Telephone Company Foreman No.401 by alleged strikers.

Made by D.P.S. Watman. Forwarded by [Signature] O'Brien

20/6/32
At 11.10 a.m./in response to a telephone message from Mr Thorley of the Shanghai Telephone Co., the undersigned and Chinese detectives proceeded to the Yee Zu Li (怡如里), off Tong Dong Ka Loong, from which place one Ts Vai Tsong (朱美昌), Foreman No.401 of the company was reported to have been abducted by some alleged strikers.

Enquiries show that at 10.30 a.m. even date, this foreman was working in the Yee Zu Li, in charge of a party of thirteen workmen when seven or eight men entered and having ascertained that he was in charge of the party, escorted the foreman from the alleyway and proceeded via North Shanse Road to Ningpo Road where after striking him several times, the men released the foreman with threats of further violence if he persisted in working.

In the meantime, Chinese detectives were detailed to make enquiries at all places in the district to which the foreman might have been taken and also at the home of this man, these enquiries were without result but at 2.00 p.m. the foreman came to the station and gave his version of the affair as above.

A statement has been taken from the foreman and he was closely questioned by D.S.I. Gash and the undersigned as to the identity of the men concerned in the abduction but states that he has never before seen the men and does not know whether they were strikers or merely loafers engaged to terrorise those attempting to work.

[Signature]
Senior Detective;

D. Harman
D.P.S.

D.D.O. "C" Div.
O. i/c Special Branch.

事由（全称）关于上海电话公司领班第401号被 alleged strikers（疑似罢工者）绑架一事。

由警佐沃特曼（Watman）呈报。经奥布莱恩（O'Brien）[签名] 转呈

1932年6月20日
上午11时10分/应上海电话公司索利先生（Mr Thorley）的电话通知，具名人与华探前往同德卡龙（Tong Dong Ka Loong）旁的怡如里（Yee Zu Li），据报该公司领班第401号朱美昌（Ts Vai Tsong）在此地被一些疑似罢工者绑架。

经查，当日上午10时30分，该领班正在怡如里工作，负责带领十三名工人，此时七八名男子进入，在确认他是带队负责人后，将该领班从弄堂带出，经北山西路（North Shanse Road）前往宁波路，在那里殴打他数次后，这些人释放了该领班，并威胁如果他继续工作将施加更多暴力。

与此同时，已指派华探在该地区该领班可能被带往的所有地点以及其住所进行调查，这些调查均无结果，但下午2时，该领班来到捕房，如上所述陈述了事件经过。

已对该领班取得供词，并由刑事侦缉督察加什（Gash）及具名人就参与绑架者的身份对其进行了严密讯问，但他声称以前从未见过这些人，也不知道他们是罢工者还是仅仅受雇来恐吓试图工作之人的闲散人员。

[签名]
高级侦探；

D. 哈曼（Harman）

SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE.

REPORT OF POLICE INVESTIGATIONS.

The following is the statement of Ts Vai Tsong (朱萬昌).
native of Kompo taken by me D.P.S. Warman.
translated
at W. H'kew on the 20-6-32. and interpreted by Interpreter Chu.

My name is Ts Vai Tsong, native of Kompo, age 39 and I am
a foreman No. 401 attached to the Head Telephone Co., Fokien
Road.

At 8 a.m. to-day while I was repairing the main wire in Yee
Zu Li off Tong Dong Ka Loong. At about 10.30 a.m. suddenly
7 or 8 persons probably strikers approached me and took me away
with them via Tong Dong Ka Loong and North Shanse Road towards
south and passed over Shanse Road Bridge and we then turned on
west side of Shanse Road to Ningpo Road, where they assaulted
me several times and strictly told me not to resume work and also
told me not to resume work together with others till the settle-
ment of the strike. Later I then returned to my home.

Sd. Ts Vai Tsong and cross marked.

RECORD OF INVESTIGATION.

SHANGHAI TELEPHONE COMPANY'S OUTDOOR STAFF - FOKIEN ROAD EXCHANGE.

There is no change in the strike situation of the above Company.

At 9.50 a.m. June 17 a telephone message was received from Mr. Thorley of the Fokien Road Exchange to the effect that a nail had been found driven into a telephone cable in the Dzanq Lin Ka alleyway (曾林卡弄堂), Fokien Road disconnecting 50 lines. Subsequent inquiries revealed that at 2 a.m. June 13 about four or five men dressed in blue cotton clothing entered the above alleyway where one of their number stood on a ledge of the wall and drove a nail into the cable, with a short iron bar, at a point about 8 feet from the ground. His action was observed by two assistants employed in a food stall at the entrance to the alleyway, who however were unable to give a useful description of the men. These two assistants named Yue Vung Ziang (俞鳳祥) and Wong Ah Mei (黃阿美) were taken to the Fokien Road Exchange at 3 p.m. and shown the photographs of many of the outdoor staff but were unable to identify any of them.

In consequence of this information special plain clothes patrols have been put on night duty.

French Tramway Company Employees' Club
The eleven standing committee members and five
supervisory committee members of the French Tramway
Company Employees' Club who were elected during an
inaugural meeting held on June 15 assumed their posts at
6 p.m. June 16 in their office, 1st floor, 244 Rue Kraetzer.

N.W.K. No.5 Mill, 14 W/Soochow Road
At 4.35 p.m. June 16, a male pump room worker named
Zung Nyeh Ziang (张聂祥) of the N.W.K. No.5 Cotton Mill
entered the Ring Spinning Room of the mill in question and
switched off one or two machines there as a protest
against the dismissal of his friend Wong Tseu Sung (王祖松)
employed in the same mill. He was escorted off the
premises by Municipal Police and the machines were restarted
about five minutes later, without further incident.

The strike situation remains unchanged.
At 10 a.m. June 16 about 200 workers led by a
foreman named Yao Ngo-sung (姚五松) of the "New
Fitting Room" appeared at the Fokien Road Exchange and
expressed their willingness to resume work as they
understood the Company had accepted five of their
demands. On being told by the Manager that none of
their demands had been accepted they refused to resume
work, but stated that they were willing to work at once
and shelve the question of demands, provided the Company

法商电车公司职员俱乐部
法商电车公司职员俱乐部在6月15日举行的成立大会上选出的十一名常务委员和五名监察委员，于6月16日下午6时在克拉策尔路（Rue Kraetzer）244号一楼的办公室就职。

西北纺织株式会社第五厂，苏州河西14号
6月16日下午4时35分，西北纺织株式会社第五棉纺厂一名名叫张聂祥（Zung Nyeh Ziang）的男泵房工人进入该厂的环锭纺纱间，关闭了那里的一两台机器，以抗议其在该厂工作的朋友王祖松（Wong Tseu Sung）被解雇。他被工部局警察带离厂区，机器在五分钟后重新启动，未发生进一步事件。

上海电话公司 - 工人罢工
罢工局势保持不变。
6月16日上午10时，约200名工人在一名名叫姚五松（Yao Ngo-sung）的“新装配间”领班的带领下出现在福建路交换台，并表示愿意恢复工作，因为他们理解公司已接受他们的五项要求。当经理告知他们任何要求都未被接受时，他们拒绝恢复工作，但表示如果公司

would recognize the Union as representing the workers. On
this request being rejected by the Manager, the visitors took
their departure. When the workers arrived at the corner of
Foochow and Hupch Roads, they assaulted the foreman who,
they alleged, had deceived them regarding the Company
having made concessions, and which had caused them to turn
up for work. The foreman however succeeded in getting away
without much injury.

On the forenoon of June 16, a letter was received at the
Communication Address of the Strike Committee. This letter
purporting to emanate from the Eastern District Cotton Mill
Workers' Union promised full support to the strike. Another
letter of a similar nature was received from the National
Salvation Committee of the Students of the Chinese Public
School, 1260 Rue Lafayette on June 15.

The following five reports of telephone cables being
found cut or otherwise interfered with were recorded on June
16. In all cases the necessary repairs were quickly effected:
On the morning of June 16 a wire nail was found driven
through a telephone cable in Tong Sung Li, Chekiang Road,
thereby disconnecting 60 lines.
At 9.55 a.m. a telephone cable was found cut in Foh
Tsong Li, Yunnan Road, disconnecting 14 lines.
At 2.35 p.m. a cable located in Ming Ching Li, Kiukieng
Road, was found cut, 40 lines being disconnected.
During the afternoon two wire nails were found
driven into a telephone cable in the Tung An Li, Hankow Road,
15 lines being disconnected.
In the forenoon a cable in the Ming Yih Li, Kiukieng.
Road, was found to have been cut.

6月16日上午，罢工委员会联络处收到一封信。这封信自称来自东区棉纺工人工会，承诺全力支持此次罢工。另一封类似性质的信于6月15日来自霞飞路（Rue Lafayette）1260号中国公学学生救国会。

2nd District (French Concession) Waterworks and Electricity
Workers' Union - Meeting

25 committee members of the above Union held a meeting
in their office, 23 Dah Teh Li, Loo Pen Road, Nantao, opposite
Avenue Dubail, between 5 and 7.30 p.m. June 15 when Tsou Teh
Shing (邹德兴) who was appointed to negotiate with the Company
to continue the issue of a monthly subsidy of $200.00 to the
Union, etc. (Vide I.R. 13/6/32) reported that the Company
when interviewed at 5.30 p.m. June 14, promised to refer their
request to its General Office in Paris while in connection with
the demand for the release of Hsu Ah Mei the Company announced
that it is not in a position to consider the case, although
it is sure that Hsu is not a communist and advised them to
take legal proceedings in the matter. The following resolutions
were then discussed and passed:-

1. That the rumour now current to the effect that the workers
of the French Tramway Company will declare a strike be
repudiated by inserting an advertisement in the local press
on June 17.

2. That the Social Bureau and local Kuomintang be requested
by letter to certify that Hsu Ah Mei is not a communist.

The meeting was presided by one Tsai Ah Mei. (蔡阿梅).

Shanghai Telephone Company Workers - Strike

The strike situation remains unchanged.

Six representatives of the strikers (senior grades) are
expected to call at the Company's office, Kiangsi Road,
this forenoon to discuss further the amended demands submitted
on June 14.

There are indications that dissension has arisen in the
ranks of the strikers who are now in two cliques, i.e. the
seniors who appear to be ready to resume work provided the
Company will give them "face" by granting some small

第二区（法租界）水电工人联合会——会议

上述联合会的25名委员于6月15日下午5时至7时30分，在南市鲁班路达德里23号（杜美路对面）的办事处举行会议。会上，被指派与公司谈判以继续向联合会每月发放200.00美元津贴等事宜的邹德兴（Tsou Teh Shing）报告称（参见1932年6月13日情报报告），公司于6月14日下午5时30分接受问询时，承诺将其请求转呈巴黎总公司；至于释放徐阿梅（Hsu Ah Mei）的要求，公司宣布无法考虑此案，尽管其确信徐并非共产党员，并建议他们就此采取法律程序。随后讨论并通过以下决议：-

1. 针对目前流传的法商电车公司工人将举行罢工的谣言，将于6月17日在当地报刊刊登广告予以否认。

2. 致函社会局及当地国民党，请求证明徐阿梅并非共产党员。

会议由蔡阿梅（Tsai Ah Mei）主持。

上海电话公司工人——罢工

罢工局势保持不变。

六名罢工者代表（高级职员）预计将于今天上午前往江西路公司办公室，进一步讨论6月14日提交的修订后要求。

有迹象表明，罢工队伍内部出现分歧，目前分为两派：即高级职员派，他们似乎准备在公司给予某些微小让步以顾全其“面子”的情况下复工；以及低级职员派，其中包含更为激进的分子，据信切断或破坏电话电缆以使公司陷入困境的企图背后即是此派人马，他们的政策是持续并加剧罢工，直至最初的要求得到满足。

concession, and the juniors amongst whom are the more radical
elements who are thought to be behind attempts to embarrass the
Company by cutting or otherwise damaging telephone cables
and whose policy is to carry on and intensify the strike until
the original demands have been met.

At 5.30 p.m. a striker named Tang Liang-tsz (唐亮之)
was assaulted on Boulevard de Montigny by three unknown
Chinese. He, however, made good his escape with but slight
injury. It appears that the victim was until recently a
member of the Strike Committee, which is comprised of lower
grade workers and which the Company persists in refusing to
recognize, but has now thrown in his lot with the seniors.

The following three cases of cable cutting came to
the notice of the Company on June 15 and in each instance
repairs were immediately effected :-

Between 9 p.m. June 12 and 8 a.m. June 15 a cable
located in Foh Ts Li, Kwangse Road was cut, disconnecting 51
lines.

On the morning of June 15 a cable in Poo Ching Li,
Foochow Road, was similarly damaged, thereby affecting 41
lines.

The same morning a cable was cut in Tong Shing Li,
Foochow Road, disconnecting 60 lines.

The different kinds of handbills addressed to
Striking Workers of the Telephone Company and purporting to
emanate from the Propaganda Department of the Shanghai Central
District Committee of the Chinese Communist Party, respectively,
were thrown into Nanking Road from Sincere Roof Garden at
9.05 p.m. June 15. These leaflets urge the strikers to
persist in their demands and state that the electricity
workers of the Settlement, French Concession and Chinese
Territory are about to declare a strike in their support.

Shanghai Telephone Company's Employees
strike - Fokien Road Exchange.

It now appears that the majority of the strikers
of the above company are willing to resume work provided
the company make some small concession. The Company
however refuse to discuss terms until the men resume
work.

Three reports of Telephone cables being cut in
this district were received on June 15th as under.

1. Between 9 p.m. June 12, and 8 a.m. June 13, a telephone
cable situated in the Fon Za Li alleyway (福致里),
Kwangsi Road was cut and 51 lines disconnected.
This cable runs parallel with the alleyway about 10
feet from the ground and passes a watchman's room
situated over the entrance to the alleyway and near
to a staircase leading to the room. The culprit
evidently climbed the stairs to cut the cable which

12 noon June 14, 1932.
from Supt. Robertson.

Shanghai Telephone Company - Strike of Mechanics

At 9 a.m. June 14, six representatives
of the Senior Staff of the Shanghai Telephone Company,
who have a communication address in Rooms 513 and 518
Far Eastern Hotel, Pakhoi and Thibet Roads corner,
called at the Fokien Road Exchange and submitted to
the Manager the following curtailed list of demands :-

1. That no workers be dismissed without reason and
that any worker to be dismissed be given a retiring
gratuity equivalent to 2 months' wages as well as
his superannuation monies.

2. That all workers especially those receiving less than
$40 per month be granted an annual increase.

3. That wages be issued for the period of strike.

4. That wages be issued for holidays as well as leave
for weddings or funerals and that double wages be
issued to those who work on Sundays and holidays.

5. That one month's bonus be issued to all workers at
the end of each year.

6. That compensation be issued in the case of workers
injured or killed in the execution of their duty.

The Manager of the Exchange promised to give a reply at
3 p.m. to-day.

It is reported that delegates of the strikers
of grades lower than the above mentioned seniors plan to
call on the General Manager of the Company at Kiangsi
Road Office at 2 p.m. to-day.

（批：14/6）

上海电话公司 - 技工罢工

1932年6月14日上午9时，上海电话公司高级职员的六名代表（通讯地址为北海路与西藏路转角远东饭店513和518室）前往福建路交换局，并向经理提交了以下精简后的要求清单：-

1. 不得无故解雇工人，任何被解雇的工人应获得相当于两个月工资的遣散费以及其养老金。

2. 所有工人，特别是月薪低于40美元的工人，应获得年度加薪。

3. 罢工期间应发放工资。

4. 节假日以及婚丧假期间应发放工资，周日和节假日工作者应发放双倍工资。

5. 每年年底应向所有工人发放一个月的奖金。

6. 工人在执行职务时受伤或死亡，应给予赔偿。

交换局经理承诺于今天下午3时给予答复。

据报道，级别低于上述高级职员的罢工者代表计划于今天下午2时前往江西路办公室拜访公司总经理。

The attitude of the strikers of the above Company seems to be less radical and they now appear to be divided into two friendly groups consisting of "old" and "new" employes.

At 8.30.a.m. June 14, a delegation of 6 "old" employes representing the Maintenance (2) Installation, Construction, Education and Engineering Divisions submitted to Mr. Wilson 6 demands, a copy of which has been sent to the Special Branch, as a basis for the resumption of work. They were requested to see Mr. Wilson again at 3.p.m. and after a consultation with him which finished at 5.p.m. he informed them that their demands would be considered when they resumed work.

About 20 of the men of strike have engaged Rooms 513 and 518 of the Far Eastern Hotel, 30 Pakhoi Road and are using them as an Intelligence Centre. The rooms were engaged in the name of Wong Yih Ming (王一民).

Between 4 and 6.p.m. two members of the Shanghai Labour Union entertained to tea in the Hang Hwo Lur Restaurant, 526 Foochow Road seven reporters of various local Mosquito newspapers but the topic discussed is not known. One of the hosts was Yih Koong Tsan (葉公照).
