page_data.en:
List of literature contained in a parcel received
by mail by the Shanghai Telephone Company on
13/6/32. The parcel is addressed to the
"Shanghai Telephone Company Strike Committee".

----------

1. A copy of a leaflet purporting to emanate from the
"National Salvation Federation of the Shanghai
Masses to Resist Japan" and dated June 12. The
literature is entitled "Oppose the Round Table
Conference" and in it opposition is made to the
Round Table Conference which is alleged to be
utilized by the Imperialists to partition Shanghai.
It further calls for the overthrow of the Kuomintang
which the literature states is the running dog
of the Imperialists.

2. Thirty-two copies of a leaflet entitled "Oppose
the Landing of Imperialists' Marines at Amoy",
purporting to have been issued by the above
mentioned Federation and bearing the same date.
The literature declares that the struggle made by
the "Red" Army is for the emancipation of the
Chinese labourers, peasants and toiling masses
and at its conclusion urges the members of the
"Red Army" and the toiling masses to come to arms
for the purpose of opposing the landing of Imperialists
Armies in Chinese territory and of disarming them
and driving away all Imperialists from China.

3. Sixteen copies of a leaflet purporting to emanate
from the "Determine-to-die" corps to Proceed to the
North in support of the North Eastern Volunteer
Army and entitled "Rise and join the Determine-to-
die Corps to proceed to the North". It contains
ten objects of the Corps, which include (a) the
driving out of the "diatrict" (China) of the
League Commission as well as the influence of any
Imperialists, (b) the giving of assistance to
the labourers in anti-Japanese struggles and demands
for increase in wages and decrease in working
hours, and (c) the confiscation of Japanese goods
and the property of Japanese Imperialists for the
support of unemployed workers, strikers, and
refugees.

4. Thirty copies of a handbill containing a manifesto
of the "National Salvation Salvation Federation
of the Shanghai Masses to Resist Japan" in support
of the strike of the telephone workers. The
paper is dated June 8. A summarized translation
of the manifesto in question is hereunder :
page_data.zh:
1932年6月13日上海电话公司通过邮件收到的包裹中所含宣传品清单。该包裹收件人为
“上海电话公司罢工委员会”。

----------

1. 一份传单副本，声称出自“上海民众抗日救国联合会”，日期为6月12日。该宣传品题为《反对圆桌会议》，其中反对所谓被帝国主义者利用来瓜分上海的圆桌会议。它还呼吁推翻国民党，该宣传品称国民党是帝国主义者的走狗。

2. 三十二份题为《反对帝国主义海军陆战队在厦门登陆》的传单副本，声称由上述联合会发布，日期相同。该宣传品宣称，“红军”进行的斗争是为了中国劳工、农民和劳苦大众的解放，并在结尾敦促“红军”成员和劳苦大众武装起来，以反对帝国主义军队在中国领土登陆，解除其武装，并将所有帝国主义者驱逐出中国。

3. 十六份传单副本，声称出自“决死队北上支援东北义勇军”，题为《起来加入决死队北上》。其中列出了该队的十项目标，包括 (a) 将国联调查团以及任何帝国主义者的势力驱逐出“diatrict”（中国），(b) 援助劳工进行抗日斗争，并提出增加工资和减少工时的要求，以及 (c) 没收日本货物和日本帝国主义者的财产，以资助失业工人、罢工者和难民。

4. 三十份传单，包含“上海民众抗日救国联合会”支持电话工人罢工的宣言。该文件日期为6月8日。有关宣言的摘要译文如下：

page_data.en:
- 2 -

Manifesto of the National Salvation Federation
of the Shanghai Masses to Resist Japan in support
of the strike of the telephone workers.

The 3,000 workers of the Shanghai Telephone
Company have gone on strike since June 7 as a protest
against the cruel oppression of the Imperialists and
capitalists. This struggle has an extra-ordinary
and great significance.
The American Imperialists and capitalists
holding a policy of economic invasion monopolize the
telephone service and put thousands of workers under
oppression. Availing themselves of the opportunity
presented by the tragedy perpetrated by the Japanese
Imperialists, which has made the people so poor, the
American Imperialists and capitalists have dismissed
several hundreds of workers and have decided to dispense
with the service of a further batch of three or four
hundred hands, to increase the work of the staff and
to engage White Russians to replace the present
workers. The annual increase to be granted every
April and Sunday work have also been abolished.
Those workers who have been in the company's service for
over 20 years only get about $20 a month. This has
pained us and aroused our anger and therefore we call
upon the toiling masses of the whole of Shanghai to
give substantial assistance to the telephone strikers
in their brave struggle. Let us collect contributions
for their support, send some body to them and console
them, encourage them and organize and extend the strike
so as to increase their power of struggle.
From the fact that the Imperialists, the
traitorous Government and capitalists are surrounding
us from all sides and violently attacking us, and that
they are contemplating the holding of a round table
conference to establish the Shanghai Free City and
the public control of Manchuria, and from the oppression
on workers shown recently in the China Times, Commercial
Press, Wing On Cotton Mill, the Public Ricshas, the
Yoong Chong Match Factory, the Kiwa Mills, conclusion
can be easily drawn that unless we, the toiling masses,
unite and use our own power to persist in the struggle,
we shall have no way to emancipation. Do not listen
to the words of labour traitors and running dogs, such
as "To strike disturbs the peace and good order of
society". Let us ignore these deceitful works and
bravely carry on the struggle and never stop until the
last victory has been gained.
Labourers ! The Masses ! Do not imagine
any more that the American Imperialists treat China well !
From now on you must understand that U.S.A. is a bloody
and monstrous Imperialists. Rise and decidedly
struggle against the Imperialists, the capitalists
and their running dog, the traitorous Government ! Down
with these blood sucking devils ! Beasts, emancipate us !"

上海民众抗日救国联合会支持电话工人罢工的宣言。

上海电话公司的3000名工人自6月7日起罢工，以抗议帝国主义者和资本家的残酷压迫。这场斗争具有非凡且重大的意义。
奉行经济侵略政策的美国帝国主义者和资本家垄断了电话服务，使成千上万的工人遭受压迫。他们利用日本帝国主义者制造的悲剧致使民穷财尽的机会，解雇了数百名工人，并决定再裁减三四百名员工，增加在职人员的工作量，并雇佣白俄取代现有工人。每年四月发放的加薪和周日工作也已取消。那些在公司服务超过20年的工人每月仅得约20元。这令我们痛心并激起我们的愤怒，因此我们呼吁全上海的劳苦大众给予电话罢工者实质性的援助，支持他们的英勇斗争。让我们募集捐款支持他们，派人慰问和鼓励他们，并组织并扩大罢工，以增强他们的斗争力量。
鉴于帝国主义者、卖国政府和资本家正从四面八方包围并猛烈攻击我们，且他们正策划召开圆桌会议以建立上海自由市并对满洲实行公共管制，加之近期在《字林西报》、商务印书馆、永安棉纺厂、公共人力车、永昌火柴厂、日华纱厂等处对工人的压迫，不难得出结论：除非我们劳苦大众团结起来，运用自身力量坚持斗争，否则我们将无法获得解放。不要听信诸如“罢工扰乱社会和平与秩序”之类的工贼和走狗的言论。让我们无视这些欺骗性的言辞，勇敢地进行斗争，直至取得最后胜利才停止。
工人们！民众们！不要再以为美国帝国主义者善待中国！从现在起你们必须明白，美国是一个血腥且 monstrous 的帝国主义者。起来，坚决同帝国主义者、资本家及其走狗——卖国政府作斗争！打倒这些吸血魔鬼！野兽们，解放我们吧！”

List of literature contained in a parcel received
by mail by the Shanghai Telephone Company on
13/6/32. The parcel is addressed to the
"Shanghai Telephone Company Strike Committee".

1. A copy of a leaflet purporting to emanate from the
"National Salvation Federation of the Shanghai
Masses to Resist Japan" and dated June 12. The
literature is entitled "Oppose the Round Table
Conference" and in it opposition is made to the
Round Table Conference which is alleged to be
utilized by the Imperialists to partition Shanghai.
It further calls for the overthrow of the Kuomintang
which the literature states is the running dog
of the Imperialists.

2. Thirty-two copies of a leaflet entitled "Oppose
the landing of Imperialists' Marines at Amoy",
purporting to have been issued by the above
mentioned Federation and bearing the same date.
The literature declares that the struggle made by
the "Red" Army is for the emancipation of the
Chinese labourers, peasants and toiling masses
and at its conclusion urges the members of the
"Red Army" and the toiling masses to come to arms
for the purpose of opposing the landing of Imperialist
Armies in Chinese territory and of disarming them
and driving away all Imperialists from China.

3. Sixteen copies of a leaflet purporting to emanate
from the "Determine-to-die" corps to Proceed to the
North in support of the North Eastern Volunteer
Army and entitled "Rise and join the 'Determine-to-
die Corps to proceed to the North". It contains
ten objects of the Corps, which include (a) the
driving out of the "district" (China) of the
League Commission as well as the influence of any
Imperialists, (b) the giving of assistance to
the labourers in anti-Japanese struggles and demands
for increase in wages and decrease in working
hours, and (c) the confiscation of Japanese goods
and the property of Japanese Imperialists for the
support of unemployed workers, strikers, and
refugees.

4. Thirty copies of a handbill containing a manifesto
of the "National Salvation Federation
of the Shanghai Masses to Resist Japan" in support
of the strike of the telephone workers. The

1932年6月13日上海电话公司通过邮件收到的包裹中所含宣传品清单。该包裹收件人为
“上海电话公司罢工委员会”。

1. 一份传单副本，声称出自“上海民众抗日救国联合会”，日期为6月12日。该宣传品题为《反对圆桌会议》，其中反对所谓被帝国主义者利用来瓜分上海的圆桌会议。它还呼吁推翻国民党，该宣传品称国民党是帝国主义者的走狗。

2. 三十二份题为《反对帝国主义海军陆战队在厦门登陆》的传单副本，声称由上述联合会发布，日期相同。该宣传品宣称，“红军”进行的斗争是为了中国劳工、农民和劳苦大众的解放，并在结尾敦促“红军”成员和劳苦大众武装起来，以反对帝国主义军队在中国领土登陆，解除其武装，并将所有帝国主义者驱逐出中国。

3. 十六份传单副本，声称出自“决死队北上支援东北义勇军”，题为《起来加入‘决死队北上’》。其中列出了该队的十项目标，包括 (a) 将国联调查团以及任何帝国主义者的势力驱逐出“district”（中国），(b) 援助劳工进行抗日斗争，并提出增加工资和减少工时的要求，以及 (c) 没收日本货物和日本帝国主义者的财产，以资助失业工人、罢工者和难民。

4. 三十份传单，包含“上海民众抗日救国联合会”支持电话工人罢工的宣言。该文件日期为6月8日。有关宣言的摘要译文如下：

page_data.en:
Manifesto of the National Labour Federation
of the Shanghai Branch to Resist Japan in support
of the strike of the telephone workers.

The 3,000 workers of the Shanghai Telephone
Company have gone on strike since June 7 as a protest
against the cruel oppression of the Imperialists and
capitalists. This struggle has an extra-ordinary
and great significance.
The American Imperialists and capitalists
holding a policy of economic invasion monopolize the
telephone service and put thousands of workers under
oppression. Availing themselves of the opportunity
presented by the tragedy perpetrated by the Japanese
Imperialists, which has made the people so poor, the
American Imperialists and capitalists have dismissed
several hundreds of workers and have decided to dispense
with the service of a further batch of three or four
hundred hands, to increase the work of the staff and
to engage White Russians to replace the present
workers. The annual increase to be granted every
April and Sunday work have also been abolished.
Those workers who have been in the company's service for
over 20 years only get about $20 a month. This has
pained us and aroused our anger and therefore we call
upon the toiling masses of the whole of Shanghai to
give substantial assistance to the telephone strikers
in their brave struggle. Let us collect contributions
for their support, send some body to them and console
them, encourage them and organize and extend the strike
so as to increase their power of struggle.
From the fact that the Imperialists, the
traitorous Government and capitalists are surrounding
us from all sides and violently attacking us, and that
they are contemplating the holding of a round table
conference to establish the Shanghai Free City and
the public control of Manchuria, and from the oppression
on workers shown recently in the China Times, Commercial
Press, Sing On Cotton Mill, the Public Works, the
Yoong Chong Match Factory, the King Mills, conclusion
can be easily drawn that unless we, the toiling masses,
unite and use our own power to persist in the struggle,
we shall have no way to emancipation. Do not listen
to the words of labour traitors and running dogs, such
as "To strike disturbs the peace and good order of
society". Let us ignore these deceitful words and
resolutely carry on the struggle and never stop until the
last victory has been gained.
Labourers ! The Masses ! Do not imagine
any more that the American Imperialists treat China well !
From now on you must understand that U.S.A. is a bloody
and monstrous Imperialists. Rise and decidedly
struggle against the Imperialists, the capitalists
and their running dog, the traitorous Government ! Down
with these blood sucking devils ! Beasts, emancipate us !

Ex-Workers of China Times - Released

The 22 ex-workers of the China Times who were arrested by the
Public Safety Bureau on June 8 at the Press Workers Union, 14 Siao
Tac Yuen Ka, City, were released on security promised by the Press
Workers Union on June 11.

Kung Dah No.2 Cotton Mill -- Strike of workers in Carding Department

42 workers in the Carding Department of the Kung Dah No.2
Cotton Mill, 540 Yangtszepoo Road failed to start work at 6 a.m.
to-day, June 13, as a protest against the management transferring
two of their colleagues to another department of the Mill.

Shanghai Telephone Company - Strike Situation

The strike situation remains unchanged.

At 3.15 p.m. June 12, four Chinese claiming to represent
the strikers called on the management of the Company in the Fokien
Road Exchange, when the latter gave them copies of a notice
containing a reply of the Company to the petition submitted by
the strikers on June 9. The following is translation of the
notice in question :-

"On June 9, Shanghai Telephone Company received two documents
"purporting to come from a body calling itself Shanghai Telephone
"Company Workmen's Strike Committee; in one of these documents the
"reasons for the present strike of workers are set out as follows:-

1. The Company did not reward the conduct of the workmen
who continued work during the recent hostilities.

2. The Company abolished the rule regarding Sunday work
and April increases.

3. The Company dismissed a great number of workers not only
without compensation but has denied them participation
in the superannuation fund, this fund being confiscated.

4. The Company is planning to employ White Russians in
the place of Chinese.

《字林西报》前雇员 - 获释

6月8日在市内小桃源街14号印刷工人联合会被捕的22名《字林西报》前雇员，于6月11日由印刷工人联合会提供担保后获释。

公大第二棉纺厂 - 梳棉部工人罢工

位于杨树浦路540号的公大第二棉纺厂梳棉部的42名工人，为抗议管理层将其两名同事调往工厂另一部门，于今日（6月13日）上午6时未开工。

上海电话公司 - 罢工局势

罢工局势保持不变。

6月12日下午3时15分，四名自称代表罢工者的华人前往福建路交换局的公司管理处，后者向他们提供了包含公司于6月9日对罢工者提交的请愿书之回复的通知副本。该通知译文如下：

“6月9日，上海电话公司收到两份文件，
“声称来自一个自称‘上海电话公司工人罢工委员会’的组织；其中一份文件列出了
“当前工人罢工的原因如下：

1. 公司未对在近期敌对行动期间继续工作的工人的表现给予奖励。

2. 公司取消了关于星期日工作及四月加薪的规定。

3. 公司解雇了大量工人，不仅未给予补偿，还剥夺了他们参与养老金的权利，该基金已被没收。

4. 公司计划雇佣白俄取代中国人。

"On these grounds it is stated that the workers declared a strike
"at 7 p.m. on June 7 and it is to be noted that no advance notice
"of such action was given to the Company.
"       It is alleged that because of these reasons the Workers
"abandoned the service of the Public and having ceased work now
"make certain demands.
"       In reply to the above charges, made against the Company :-
"1. a. The Company paid full wages to many workers for days on
which they could not return to work due to the hostilities.
b. During the hostilities nearly double the usual amount of
overtime money was paid to the workers.
c. Many workers were given food free of cost.
d. Many workers and their families were housed by the Company.
"2. a. The greater part of the reduction in Sunday overtime pay
is due to the progress of the reconstruction programme.
b. An increase in April was not given because the general
state of business did not make this possible.
"3. The reduction in the number of workers is due to the progress
of the reconstruction programme. The Workers received the
money due to them under the rules of the Superannuation Fund,
and in addition to this they received more than the Company
was obligated to pay.
"4. The Company did not have, and at present does not have, any
plan to employ White Russians in the place of Chinese.
"       The Company cannot recognize the Union, and the Company will
"not conduct matters concerning the workmen and the Company through
"the Union.
"       The workers have been greatly misled by mischievous persons;
"many of the demands are impossible to meet; some have nothing
"whatever to do with the workers who have left their duties, and
"some of the statements made in the documents are untrue.
"       The workers have failed seriously in their plain duty to
"the Public in that they have left their posts without notice,
"without taking care of the public service and, still worse, in

c. 许多工人获得了免费食物。
d. 公司为许多工人及其家属提供了住宿。
“2. a. 星期日加班费的大幅减少是由于重建计划的推进所致。
b. 未发放四月加薪是因为总体商业状况使得此举不可行。
“3. 工人数量的减少是由于重建计划的推进。工人们已根据养老金基金规则收到了应得的款项，此外，他们收到的金额超过了公司义务支付的数额。

"service. The Company does not believe that its workers are in

later on.

Ong Tseng-hwa (翁振華 ) (Paoting Road Exchange)

Liu Chien-yoong (劉建勇 ) (Route Pichon Exchange).
Pan Ching-chuen (潘清泉 ), who claimed to be employed

“       鉴于公司相信工人已被误导，且在此解释下他们将不再同情煽动者的努力，公司呼吁其工人立即复工。公司始终愿意会见工人，并首先通过公司组织的常规渠道考虑他们提出的任何问题；管理层将与工人“面对面”讨论影响他们的问题，并努力做出任何可能且公平的调整。
“       但是，那十二名在四个交换局擅离职守并导致设备受损的工人已被解雇。”

这些自封的代表表达了不满，结束时，其中一位来自保定路（路边）交换局的名为翁振华（Ong Tseng-hwa）的人暗示，如果管理层拒绝接受承认其工会的要求，罢工将难以解决。然而，这些代表承诺将通知中包含的声明传达给工人，并在稍后给公司答复。

四位代表的姓名如下：

翁振华（Ong Tseng-hwa）（保定路交换局）
钟露洁（Zung Loo-jih）（蒙蒂尼大道交换局）
刘建勇（Liu Chien-yoong）（毕勋路交换局）。
潘清泉（Pan Ching-chuen），声称受雇于电线修理部，由一名名为 Zan Loo 的领班管理并支付薪水。

page_data.en:
June 13, 1932.

Labour (5)

Ong Tseng-hwa, the first mentioned delegate', also claimed
to be the President of the Strike Committee and during the
deliberations with the management of the Fokien Road Exchange
persisted in employing the word "masses" when referring to the
"workers" or "employees" which would usually be employed. The
management could not identify the last named delegate as a worker
of the Company. According to the delegates, no labour union has
been established except the Strike Committee of eleven which was
elected some time before the commencement of the strike at a
meeting attended by some 40/50 representatives of the Company's staff.

Between 1 and 3 p.m. June 11, about 200 strikers held a
meeting in the Loo Tsung Koh Teashop, 381/2 Chekiang Road, when
it was decided to continue the strike until June 13 and in the
event of no satisfactory reply being received from the Company
by that date, to decide, on more extensive measures.

It is reported that the strikers are without funds and are
receiving financial support from the Postal Workers' Union.

On the afternoon of June 12, two nails were discovered
driven through a cable in an alleyway opposite the Strand Theatre,
Ningpo Road. Repairs were immediately effected.

About 200 strikers held a meeting between 9.30 and 10.30
a.m. to-day, June 13, in the Sab Tsong Koh Teashop, 578 Chekiang
Road, to discuss the matter of selecting pickets. No decision
was reached and the meeting will be continued this afternoon on
the Chinan University temporary premises, 56 Hart Road. During
the meeting leaflets entitled "2nd Manifesto of the Telephone
Company Workers" were distributed.
page_data.zh:
1932年6月13日。

劳工 (5)

上述第一位代表翁振华还声称自己是罢工委员会主席，在与福建路交换局管理层的商议过程中，在提及通常使用的“工人”或“雇员”时，坚持使用“群众”一词。管理层无法确认最后一位代表为公司员工。据代表们称，除罢工开始前一段时间在一次约有40至50名公司员工代表参加的会议上选出的十一人罢工委员会外，尚未成立任何工会。

6月11日下午1时至3时之间，约200名罢工者在浙江路381/2号的陆宗合茶室举行会议，决定罢工持续至6月13日，若在该日期前未收到公司的满意答复，则决定采取更广泛的措施。

据报道，罢工者资金匮乏，正接受邮政工人联合会的财政支持。

6月12日下午，在宁波路 Strand 剧院对面的一条小巷里，发现一根电缆被钉入两枚钉子。随即进行了修复。

今日（6月13日）上午9时30分至10时30分之间，约200名罢工者在浙江路578号的萨宗合茶室举行会议，讨论选拔纠察队事宜。未达成决定，会议将于今天下午在哈特路56号的暨南大学临时校舍继续举行。会议期间分发了题为《电话公司工人第二宣言》的传单。

REPORT OF INTERVIEW WITH STRIKING WORKERS OF THE SHANGHAI POWER COMPANY
Police Interpreter

The following persons attending were:

Ong Tseng-hua (                ) of the Pootung Road Automatic
Tang Lee-jih  (                ) of the Boulevard Montigny Automatic
Liu Chien-yoong (              ) of the Sichen Road Automatic
Pao Ching-chun (               ) of the Wire Repairing Dept.
under the control of and paid by foreign co. loo.

They claimed to be part of the Strike Committee of eleven elected meeting before the
breakout of the strike at a meeting attended by some 40/50 representatives of the
Company staff (each division about 3/4 representative).    No labour union has yet
been established, but the Strike Committee.

After reading the notice given them, they replied that the answer contained in the
notice was too vague and was not an answer to the workers' demands.

At first they dwelt upon the importance of the organization of a labour union which
according to them will maintain mutual friendship between the capital and labour.
They also demanded that the Management should not dismiss the 18 workers mentioned
in the Notice.   They said that the blame should not be cast on the workers, but
the watchman who, it is alleged, allowed strangers to enter the premises to do
damage.   One of the attendance named Liu Chien-yoong of the Sichen Road Automatic
said that at 6 p.m. June 7 four strangers gained admission into the premises and
intimidated him by pointing pistols at him.   He, however, succeeded in shutting
the gates of the premises thus avoiding the damage of Company equipment, by
consenting to follow them out.

Then they interrogated why the Management did not give them an answer to the eighteen
demands of the Workers submitted to the Management last year.   They said that they
were working at the time of submitting the demands and the Company took no heed.
this they said constitutes one of the reasons for this present strike.   They too
asserted that they experience too much difficulty in their living conditions due to
the bad treatment of the Company which compels them to strike.

One of the attendance named Ong Tseng-hua remonstrated against a paragraph in the Company's
Notice regarding the deceit of workers by bad elements by claiming that the strike is
supported by the whole body of the workers and insisting on that the strike was de-
clared by the workers themselves and how the thousands of workers can be cheated by
only several persons.   He concluded by charging the Management of ignoring the
interests of the employees, and taking oppressive measures against them.

At the conclusion of the proceedings Ong Tseng-hua intimated that should the Manage-
ment refuse to accept the demand for recognition of their labour union, the strike
could hardly be settled.   These self-styled representatives however promised to convey
the statement contained in the Notice to the workers and to give an answer to the
Company later on.

Ong Tseng-hwa, during the conversation spoke the word "masses" instead of "workers or
employees" which he should say.   He claims to be the President of the Strike Committee.

他们声称自己是罢工委员会的一部分，该委员会由十一名当选成员组成，是在罢工爆发前的一次会议上选出的，出席会议的有约40至50名公司员工代表（每个部门约3至4名代表）。目前尚未成立工会，只有罢工委员会。

在阅读发给他们的通告后，他们回答说，通告中的答复过于含糊，并非对工人要求的回应。

起初，他们着重阐述了组织工会的重要性，据他们称，这将维持资方与劳方之间的友好关系。他们还要求管理层不得解雇通告中提到的18名工人。他们说，责任不应归咎于工人，而应归咎于看守人，据称该看守人允许陌生人进入场所进行破坏。出席者之一、四川路自动交换台的刘建勇说，6月7日下午6时，四名陌生人获准进入场所，并用枪指着他进行恐吓。然而，他通过同意随他们离开，成功关上了场所的大门，从而避免了公司设备受损。

接着，他们质问管理层为何不对去年提交给管理层的工人十八项要求给予答复。他们说，在提出要求时他们正在工作，但公司未予理会。他们说，这是导致此次罢工的原因之一。他们还断言，由于公司的恶劣待遇，他们的生活条件极其困难，这迫使他们罢工。

出席者之一翁增华对公司通告中关于不良分子欺骗工人的一段话提出异议，声称罢工得到全体工人的支持，并坚持认为罢工是由工人自己宣布的，几千名工人怎么可能仅被几个人欺骗。他最后指责管理层无视员工利益，并对他们采取压迫性措施。

会议结束时，翁增华暗示，如果管理层拒绝承认其工会的要求，罢工很难解决。然而，这些自称为代表的人承诺将通告中的声明传达给工人，并稍后给予公司答复。

翁增华在谈话中使用了“群众”一词，而不是他应该说的“工人或雇员”。他声称自己是罢工委员会主席。

page_data.en:
11 June 1932

TO THE WORKERS OF SHANGHAI TELEPHONE COMPANY

On June 9th, Shanghai Telephone Company received two documents purporting to come from a body calling itself Shanghai Telephone Company, Workmens' Strike Committee; in one of these documents the reasons for the present strike of workers are set out as follows:-

1. The Company did not reward the conduct of the workmen who continued work during the recent hostilities.
2. The Company abolished the rule regarding Sunday work and April increases.
3. The Company dismissed a great number of workers not only without compensation but has denied them participation in the superannuation fund, this fund being confiscated.
4. The Company is planning to employ White Russians in the place of Chinese.

On these grounds it is stated that the workers declared a strike at 7 p.m. on the 7th June and it is to be noted that no advance notice of such action was given to the Company.

It is alleged that because of these reasons the Workers abandoned the service of the Public and having ceased work now make certain demands.

In reply to the above charges, made against the Company:-

1. a. The Company paid full wages to many Workers for days on which they could not return to work due to the hostilities.
b. During the hostilities nearly double the usual amount of overtime money was paid to the workers.
c. Many workers were given food free of cost.
d. Many workers and their families were housed by the Company.
page_data.zh:
1932年6月11日

致上海电话公司工人

6月9日，上海电话公司收到两份文件，声称来自一个自称“上海电话公司工人罢工委员会”的组织；其中一份文件列出了工人目前罢工的原因如下：-

1. 公司未对在近期敌对行动期间坚持工作的工人的行为给予奖励。
2. 公司取消了关于周日工作和四月加薪的规定。
3. 公司解雇了大量工人，不仅没有赔偿，还剥夺了他们参与养老基金的权利，该基金被没收。
4. 公司计划雇用白俄取代中国人。

基于上述理由，据说工人于6月7日晚7时宣布罢工，值得注意的是，此前未向公司发出任何此类行动的通知。

据称，由于这些原因，工人放弃了为公众服务，在停止工作后提出某些要求。

针对上述对公司的指控，答复如下：-

1. a. 对于因敌对行动而无法返回工作岗位的日子，公司向许多工人支付了全额工资。
b. 在敌对行动期间，向工人支付的加班费几乎是平常的两倍。
c. 许多工人获得了免费食物。
d. 公司为许多工人及其家属提供了住所。

SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE
11 June 1925 REGISTRY
No. D 3728
Date 15/6/25

TO THE WORKERS OF SHANGHAI TELEPHONE COMPANY.

On June 9th, Shanghai Telephone Company received two documents
purporting to come from a body calling itself Shanghai Telephone
Company, Workmen's Strike Committee; in one of these documents the
reasons for the present strike of workers are set out as follows:-

1. The Company did not reward the conduct of the workmen
who continued work during the recent hostilities.

2. The Company abolished the rule regarding Sunday work
and April increases.

3. The Company dismissed a great number of workers not
only without compensation but has denied them participa-
tion in the superannuation fund, this fund being con-
fiscated.

4. The Company is planning to employ White Russians in the
place of Chinese.

On these grounds it is stated that the workers declared a
strike at 7 p.m. on the 7th June and it is to be noted that no
advance notice of such action was given to the Company.

It is alleged that because of these reasons the Workers aban-
doned the service of the Public and having ceased work now make
certain demands.

In reply to the above charges, made against the Company:-

1. a. The Company paid full wages to many Workers for
days on which they could not return to work due to
the hostilities.

b. During the hostilities nearly double the usual
amount of overtime money was paid to the workers.

c. Many workers were given food free of cost.

d. Many workers and their families were housed by the Company.

致上海电话公司全体工人：

6月9日，上海电话公司收到两份文件，声称来自一个自称“上海电话公司工人罢工委员会”的组织；其中一份文件列出了此次工人罢工的原因如下：-

1. 公司未对在近期敌对行动期间坚持工作的工人的表现给予奖励。

2. 公司废除了关于周日工作及四月加薪的规定。

3. 公司解雇了大量工人，不仅未给予补偿，还剥夺了他们参与养老金的权利，该基金已被没收。

4. 公司计划雇佣白俄取代中国人。

基于上述理由，据称工人们于6月7日晚7点宣布罢工，值得注意的是，此前并未向公司发出任何预先通知。

据称，由于这些原因，工人们放弃了为公众服务，并在停止工作后提出某些要求。

针对上述对公司的指控，回复如下：-

1. a. 对于因敌对行动而无法返岗工作的日子，公司向许多工人支付了全额工资。

b. 在敌对行动期间，支付给工人的加班费几乎是平时的两倍。

c. 许多工人获得了免费食物。

d. 公司为许多工人及其家属提供了住所。

RECORD OF INVESTIGATION.
Shanghai Telephone Company Exchange Employees strike- Fokien Road Exchange.
The strike situation at the Fokien Road Exchange remains unchanged but it would appear that many of the loyal employees who are willing to resume work are prevented from doing so by peaceful picketing on the part of the more adamant men on strike.
In consequence of a rumour among the strikers to the effect that certain representatives of the Telephone Company would present further demands to Mr. Wilson of the Fokien Road Exchange this a.m. about two or three hundred men collected outside the latter premises at 8.45 a.m. June 10th and conducted themselves in a somewhat boisterous manner. About 10 a.m. four of their number sought an interview with Mr. Wilson but the latter declined to see them on the grounds that the demands presented on June 9, were not yet translated. The men then repaired to the Woo Tsoong Tien teashop 426 Fokien Road where they prepared to issue armlets bearing the three characters ( ) (Picket). Their action was discovered and the armlets together with several packets of safety pins, 2 pens and an unused Chinese note book were brought to this station. About this time between 10 a.m. and 10.15 a.m. five striking employees of the Company were observed moving amongst

June 9, 1932. 12/6/32.

STRIKE OF TELEPHONE WORKERS.

The Shanghai Telephone Company has 250 office employees, 480 workers and 1,000 coolies. It has seven branch offices of which two are in the French Concession: one at No. 106 Rue Paliko and the other at No. 57 Route Pichon.

After the change into the automatic system the management have been dismissing its staff by degrees and already 1,000 have been discharged. Fearing that their services would also be dispensed with, the remaining members of the staff demanded better treatment and went on strike at 7 p.m. on June 7. There are now over 40 workers at the Central Office.

On the evening of June 7 the strikers held a meeting at Tung Faung Hotel, Rooms Nos. 388 and 349, Thibet Road. A Strike Committee of 30 members was organized. Zung Ih Ming, Wong Shaio Zung, Chang Teh Ziang, Dao Tseng Bei, Wu Ts Sun and 6 others were appointed members of the presidium of the Strike Committee. The strikers are assembling in large hotels and teashops to wait for news.

At 3 p.m. yesterday 20 members of the Strike Committee held a meeting at China Hotel, 90 Kiukiang Road. A Propaganda Section, a Correspondence Section, a Liaison Section and Picketing Groups were organized.

A general meeting should be held this afternoon to consider the following demands which will be submitted to the Company:-
(1) That no workers be dismissed, that the work be not increased, that the dismissed be reinstated.
(2) That an increase of 10% be given to whole staff as from April 1.
(3) Reinstitution of daily rest and payment of double wages for work done on holidays.
(4) That the superannuation fund be administered by the workers themselves.
(5) That the pay be issued for the period of the worker's illness.
(6) That in the event of the Company engaging new staff the former workers be given preference.
(7) That no Russians be engaged.
(8) That no increase be made in telephone charges.

Hong Tseng Hwa, Yih Keng Chao and Zung Lou Chi, the representatives of the strikers, will call at the office of the manager this afternoon to submit the demands. The strikers will give a reception to newspaper men at 10 a.m. June 10.

The attitude of the manager of the company is very firm; he has refused to receive the workers' delegates.

At midnight yesterday twenty strikers held a secret meeting at the Tong Sang Hotel, 42 Avenue Road. The Sinsa Police upon receiving information of the meeting detailed police to the place and arrested 5 persons.

At 8 a.m. June 7 three workers entered the branch office on Rue Paliko and cut the telephone wires. The French Police have placed guards at the branch offices in the French Concession.

At 4 a.m. yesterday the following circulars were found affixed to the walls of the Paliko Branch: (1) Demand an increase of pay, (2) We are struggling for our own interests, (3) Oppose the increase in telephone charges.

Note: This strike occurred suddenly and does not seem to be organized. The demands submitted to the management were drawn up on the night of June 7-8 after the strike had been declared.

电话工人罢工。

上海电话公司拥有职员250名，工人480名，苦力1,000名。该公司设有七个分局，其中两个位于法租界：一个在派立克路（Rue Paliko）106号，另一个在毕勋路（Route Pichon）57号。

改为自动交换系统后，管理层一直在逐步裁减员工，已有1,000人被解雇。由于担心自己也会被解雇，剩余员工要求改善待遇，并于6月7日晚7时举行罢工。目前中央交换台仍有40多名工人。

6月7日晚，罢工者在西藏路东方饭店（Tung Faung Hotel）388号和349号房间举行会议。组织了一个由30人组成的罢工委员会。钟益明（Zung Ih Ming，音译）、黄少宗（Wong Shaio Zung，音译）、张德祥（Chang Teh Ziang，音译）、陶增培（Dao Tseng Bei，音译）、吴祖孙（Wu Ts Sun，音译）等6人被任命为罢工委员会主席团成员。罢工者聚集在各大型旅馆和茶馆等待消息。

昨日下午3时，罢工委员会20名成员在九江路90号中国饭店举行会议。组织了宣传部、通讯部、联络部和纠察队。

今天下午将举行全体会议，审议将向公司提交的以下要求：
(1) 不得解雇任何工人，不得增加工作量，复职被解雇者。
(2) 自4月1日起，全体员工加薪10%。
(3) 恢复每日休息，节假日工作支付双倍工资。
(4) 养老金基金由工人自行管理。
(5) 工人病假期间照发工资。
(6) 若公司雇佣新员工，应优先录用原工人。
(7) 不得雇佣俄国人。
(8) 不得提高电话费。

罢工代表洪正华（Hong Tseng Hwa，音译）、叶庚朝（Yih Keng Chao，音译）和钟楼基（Zung Lou Chi，音译）将于今天下午前往经理办公室提交要求。罢工者将于6月10日上午10时招待新闻记者。

公司经理态度非常强硬；他拒绝接见工人代表。

昨晚午夜，二十名罢工者在爱多亚路（Avenue Road）42号同桑饭店（Tong Sang Hotel，音译）举行秘密会议。新闸捕房警方接到会议情报后，派遣警员前往该地，逮捕了5人。

6月7日上午8时，三名工人进入派立克路分局，切断了电话线。法国警察已在法租界内的各分局部署警卫。

昨日凌晨4时，有人在派立克路分局的墙上发现张贴了以下传单：(1) 要求加薪，(2) 我们为自身利益而斗争，(3) 反对提高电话费。

注：此次罢工发生突然，似乎并无组织。向管理层提交的要求是在6月7日至8日晚间，即罢工宣布之后拟定的。

strike - Fokien Road Exchange.

The strike situation at the Fokien Road Exchange
remains unchanged.

About 2 p.m. June 9th 1932, approximately 200

Road Exchange to whom they decided to present certain
demands, which are enumerated elsewhere in this report.

SHANGHAI TELEPHONE COMPANY EXCHANGE WORKERS STRIKE
(FOKIEN ROAD TELEPHONE EXCHANGE)

At 8.30p.m. 7-6-32, a telephone message was received from the C.C.R. reporting that the Shanghai Telephone Company Exchange Workers had gone on strike. In consequence of this information the undersigned together with C.D.S.149 and C.D.C.184 visited the Telephone Exchange situated at 321-2 Fokien Road, and from Mr. A.L. Moore, of the Telephone Company, learned that at 7.p.m. this date, the entire Chinese staff of operators at the above Exchange, about 30 in number, walked out, without previously intimating their intention to go on strike. No damage was done to the Telephone Company property at the Fokien Road Exchange by the strikers. Mr. Moore, aforesaid, stated that as far as he was aware no demands were made by the strikers, but that it was known to the Telephone Company that considerable dissatisfaction was prevalent among their employees since December, 1931, due mostly to the change over of the Company to the Automatic system of operating

brought to Station.

Made by D.S. 91 Cigarson Forwarded by W.R. Robertson C.I.

（批：For Commr Information）

Sir,

I beg to report that at 11 p.m. on the 8-6-32, S.I. Ware,
S.I. Stephenson and C.D.C. 32 brought to Station five employees
of the Shanghai Telephone Company now on strike, who were found
by the above police officers at Room 119 of the Tung Soong
Lodging House, 47 Avenue Road, being suspected that they had
gathered for the purpose of attending a meeting to discuss the
proceeds of the strike. The names and numbers of the S.T. Co.
employees are as follows:-

1. Ching Foong Sung, No. 854.
2. Sung Wei Tsung, No. 2272.
3. Chang Pau Shing, No. 575.
4. Tsoo Ling Foh, No. 110.
5. Nyi Au Ling, No. 7047.

The room was searched and about 100 pamphlets of an anti-
capitalist nature, and 5 chops bearing the characters of the
Secretary of the Strike Committee, the supervising committee of
the strike, propaganda section of the strike, succession
Section of the strike, and accounting Section of the strike, were
found.

The five persons were interrogated and stated that they had
been warned by telephone by an unknown person not to go on duty
and to go for information to the above lodging house, and that
this room was not occupied by them and also denied any knowledge
of the pamphlets or chops.

The undersigned communicated with D.S. Moore, attached to
Special Branch Headquarters, who attended and made enquiries,
when Superintendent Robertson was informed and ordered all five
above named to be cautioned and released and pamphlets and chops
to be confiscated and sent to Special Branch Headquarters.

The above named persons were released at 1 a.m. 9-6-32.

Yours obediently,
Cigarson
D.S. 91.

先生，

谨此报告，1932年6月8日晚11点，高级督察Ware、高级督察Stephenson及刑事调查科警长32号将五名目前处于罢工状态的上海电话公司雇员带至捕房。上述警员在爱文义路（Avenue Road）47号通松旅馆（Tung Soong Lodging House，音译）119室发现了这些人，怀疑他们聚集在一起开会讨论罢工事宜。这五名上海电话公司雇员的姓名及编号如下：-

1. Ching Foong Sung，编号 854。
2. Sung Wei Tsung，编号 2272。
3. Chang Pau Shing，编号 575。
4. Tsoo Ling Foh，编号 110。
5. Nyi Au Ling，编号 7047。

经搜查该房间，发现约100份具有反资本主义性质的传单，以及5枚印章，印文分别为罢工委员会秘书、罢工监理委员会、罢工宣传部、罢工继任部（原文不清，或为接续部）和罢工会计部。

经讯问，五人声称他们接到一个陌生人的电话警告，不要上岗，并前往上述旅馆获取信息；他们还声称该房间并非由他们占用，并否认知晓任何传单或印章。

签署人与隶属于特别分部总部的巡官Moore取得联系，Moore到场并进行问询，随后通知了罗伯逊警司，罗伯逊警司命令对上述五名人员予以训诫后释放，没收传单和印章并送往特别分部总部。

上述人员于1932年6月9日凌晨1点获释。

您忠实的仆人，
Cigarson
巡官 91号。

Made by D. S. Pryde. Forwarded by Chief Insp. T. Holloway

Sir,
At about 2:40 p.m. 9-6-32 a crowd of approximately 200
strikers appeared outside the Telephone Company offices on Kiangsi
Road having come from the Fokien Road Exchange. Four of their
number named Ah Zing, No. 3080, Zih Koon Tse, No. 904, F. Z. Zee,
No. 1631, mechanics and Pan Ching Chuan, No. 190 outside construc-
tion man, entered the building and informed the management that
they were a committee elected by the strikers and presented two
papers in Chinese, being the demands of the strikers. The trans-
lation of these papers are attached. (The Telephone Company Manage-
ment state this is only a rough translation, an official translation
will be obtained later). After having presented the demands the
four men left the premises and stated they would call at Fokien
Road exchange at 10 a.m. to-morrow for a reply.
The crowd dispersed in an orderly manner.

G. S. Pryde

SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE
SPECIAL BRANCH
June 9, 1932.
Intelligence Report
Labour

Shanghai Telephone Company - strike of Chinese mechanics

A lightning strike of mechanics in the various exchanges
commenced at 7 p.m. June 7 when the five night duty mechanics
of the Western Exchange quit work and their action was immediately
followed by their colleagues, in the six exchanges of the Company
in the International Settlement and two in the French Concession.
Steps were promptly taken by the Company to meet the situation with
the result that this morning despite the absence of many of the
day mechanics, the entire telephone service is operating on a
normal basis. Immediately following the declaration of a strike
it was found that the fault indicators and several wires had been
tampered with in the Western, Lucerne, Wayside and Boulevard de
Montigny Exchanges, but only to a minor degree and the defects
were quickly adjusted.

No demands have been made by the strikers and it is surmised
that their action is to demonstrate their sympathy for employees,
principally operators who have been dismissed as a result of the
installation of the automatic system. It is not known that the
mechanics had any grievance of their own, as they were not affected
by the introduction of the new system.

It is learned that since July last the services of over
2,000 employees have been dispensed with, each employee so
dismissed being granted a retiring gratuity from a provident
fund instituted by the Company when it was decided to transfer
the service to automatic.
page_data.zh:
上海公共租界工部局警务处
特别分部
1932年6月9日。
情报报告
劳工

上海电话公司 - 华籍机务员罢工

6月7日晚7时，各交换局的机务员发起突然罢工，当时西区交换局的五名夜班机务员停止工作，他们的行动立即得到该公司在国际租界内的六个交换局及法租界内两个交换局的同事响应。公司迅速采取措施应对局势，结果是，尽管许多白班机务员缺席，但今天上午整个电话服务仍正常运行。在宣布罢工后，随即发现西区、卢塞恩（Lucerne，音译）、韦赛德（Wayside，音译）和蒙蒂尼大道（Boulevard de Montigny）交换局的故障指示器和几根线路遭到破坏，但程度轻微，缺陷很快得到修复。

罢工者尚未提出任何要求，据推测，他们的行动是为了表示对被解雇员工（主要是因安装自动系统而被解雇的话务员）的同情。目前尚不知晓机务员自身有任何不满，因为他们并未受到新系统引入的影响。

据悉，自去年七月以来，已有2000多名员工被解雇，每位被解雇的员工都从公司决定转为自动服务时设立的公积金中获得了一笔退休酬金。

page_data.en:
June 9, 1932.

Labour (2)

It is possible that the strike will extend to all Chinese employees
totalling 1,950 but even then the Company will be in a position
to maintain a normal service.

The situation this morning, is regarded by the Company as
being very satisfactory as quite a number of the mechanics have
turned up for duty and normal telephone service is being maintained
without difficulty. Of a total of 400 mechanics the Company is
unable to state how many of these workers are actually on strike.

It is reported that three representatives from each exchange
of the Company held a meeting in the home of Tsai Chih-wen (蔡文),
one of the strikers at Kiu Mow Dee, City, between 2 and 5 p.m.
June 8. It was decided to instruct all strikers to contribute
40 cents each to the fund raised to defray expenses in connection
with the strike. It was further decided to warn all strikers
that any one who secretly resumes work on his own accord will be
severely dealt with. In conclusion it was agreed that four
bicycles be purchased for the use of pickets in delivering
communications.

It is reported that twenty members of the Strike Committee held
a meeting in a teashop on Avenue Road between 4 and 6 p.m. June 8
and passed the following resolutions :-

1. That three representatives be sent to interview the Manager of
of the Company at 2 p.m. June 9 to discuss the matter.

2. That a further meeting be held on June 9 (venue to be fixed later).

3. That local journalists be entertained on June 10 with a view to
enlisting their support.

4. That another manifesto be issued.
5. That propaganda work be intensified.
6. That workers of the Shanghai Power Company be warned not to
accept any job in the Shanghai Telephone Company so as to avoid
being regarded as strike-breakers.

Wong Miao-sung (王妙生), one of the number present,
presided over the function.
page_data.zh:
1932年6月9日。

劳工 (2)

罢工有可能蔓延至所有华籍员工，总数达1,950人，但即便如此，公司仍有能力维持正常服务。

公司认为今天上午的局势非常令人满意，因为相当数量的机务员已上岗，正常电话服务得以顺利维持。在总共400名机务员中，公司无法说明其中有多少工人实际上正在罢工。

据报道，6月8日下午2时至5时，公司各交换局的三名代表在位于市区的旧庙地（Kiu Mow Dee，音译）罢工者之一蔡文（Tsai Chih-wen）家中举行会议。会议决定指示所有罢工者每人向为支付罢工相关费用而筹集的基金捐款40分。会议还决定警告所有罢工者，任何擅自秘密复工的人将受到严厉处置。最后，会议同意购买四辆自行车，供纠察队传递通讯使用。

据报道，6月8日下午4时至6时，罢工委员会的二十名成员在爱文义路的一家茶馆举行会议，并通过以下决议：-

1. 派遣三名代表于6月9日下午2时会见公司经理，商讨此事。

2. 于6月9日举行进一步会议（地点待定）。

3. 于6月10日宴请本地记者，以争取他们的支持。

4. 发布另一份宣言。
5. 加强宣传工作。
6. 警告上海电力公司的工人不要接受上海电话公司的任何工作，以免被视为破坏罢工者。

出席者之一的王妙生（Wong Miao-sung）主持了此次会议。

Bubbling Well
Thursday 9th June 193 2.

FOREIGN CHILD
BITTEN BY
DOG.
At 9.40 a.m. 8-6-32, a telephone message was received
from Gordon Road Station to the effect that the daughter of
Mr. Jones, residing at 91 Seymour Road, was bitten badly by
a Police dog.
Enquiries were made by C.S.I. Chang, dog owned by Mr.
K.S. Sih of 93 Seymour Road (Alsatian dog).
Mr. Jones had already taken his daughter to Doctor for
treatment and she was afterwards taken by Police to Health
Dept. for treatment, and dog removed to Keylock and Pratt
for observation.

WALKING SEARCH
PARTY.
Between 11 p.m. 8-6-32 and 3 a.m. 9-6-32, one uniform
search party operated on various roads in the district.
12 motor cars were stopped and searched, all correct.

TELEPHONE
COMPANY
EMPLOYEES
STRIKE.
All Chinese employees of the Western Exchange, Medhurst
Road, are still on strike on 8-6-32. At 8.30 a.m. 8-6-32, the
foreigner i/c. of the Western Exchange reported that he had
heard that several linesmen proceeding to work on the company's
bicycles had been stopped on the road and their machines had
been confiscated by strikers. A patrol toured the district
with a telephone company employee but failed to observe any of
the company's bicycles on the streets.
Subsequently on receipt of information that the strikers
might cut the telephone cables, patrols scoured the district.
No trace of strikers could be found.
Nothing of unusual nature occurred in the vicinity of
this Exchange.

The female workers at the Lucerne Exchange worked as usual,
but two maintenance foremen failed to report for duty, other
employees worked as usual.
The Hungjao Exchange was working normally.

C. Bishop
Inspector i/c.

静安寺
1932年6月9日，星期四。

外籍儿童
被狗咬伤。
1932年6月8日上午9时40分，接到戈登路分局的电话消息，称居住在西摩路91号的琼斯先生（Mr. Jones）的女儿被一只警犬严重咬伤。
由刑事侦缉探员张（Chang，音译）进行调查，该狗为西摩路93号的 Sih K.S. 先生（音译）所有（阿尔萨斯狼狗）。
琼斯先生已将女儿送往医生处治疗，随后由警方将其送往卫生处接受治疗，该狗被送往基洛克和普拉特（Keylock and Pratt，音译）处进行观察。

步行搜查
小队。
1932年6月8日晚上11时至6月9日凌晨3时之间，一支制服搜查小队在该地区的各条道路上行动。
拦截并搜查了12辆汽车，一切正常。

电话
公司
雇员
罢工。
1932年6月8日，麦赫斯特路（Medhurst Road）西区交换局的所有华籍雇员仍在罢工。1932年6月8日上午8时30分，西区交换局的外籍负责人报告称，他听说几名乘坐公司自行车去上班的线路工在路上被拦下，他们的自行车被罢工者没收。一名巡警陪同一名电话公司员工在该地区巡逻，但未在街道上发现任何公司的自行车。
随后，在收到罢工者可能切断电话电缆的情报后，巡警对该地区进行了彻底搜查。未发现罢工者的踪迹。
该交换局附近未发生任何异常事件。

卢塞恩交换局的女工照常工作，但两名维修领班未报到上班，其他员工照常工作。
虹桥交换局工作正常。

C. Bishop
主管督察。

page_data.en:
Copy for Officer i/c. Spl. Branch.

Jubbling Roll
Wednesday 8th June 1932.

STRIKE OF
CHINESE
TELEPHONE
EMPLOYEES.
At 8.20 p.m. 7-6-32, a telephone message was received from
C.C.R. to the effect that the employees of the Shanghai Tele-
phone Coy. had gone strike.
Insp. Bishop and D.P.S. Crowden immediately attended to the
Western Exchange, Modhurst Road, where it was ascertained
that the night shift of 5 employees had walked out at about
7 p.m. 7-6-32 without warning. Cause of strike thought to be
intended for a raise in pay.
The day shift of 20 men is also expected to go on strike
as the Manager of the Western Exchange stated that they
expected this strike tomorrow, 8-6-32, so apparently the
movement was general. Later it was ascertained nearly all
exchanges over the Settlement were in the same position.
At the Western Exchange however the automatic system was
being run by foreign staff. A police guard of one Foreign Sergt.
and three C.P.C.s has been placed at the exchange and at the
French Exchange at Lucerne a similar guard has been placed
where the workers are carrying on for the time being.
Major Wainwright, D.O. "B" informed and attended.
Enquiries proceeding.

HARBO VAN
PATROL.
Between 11 a.m. & 1 p.m. also between 7 p.m. & 8 p.m.
7-6-32, one Radio Van patrolled various roads in the district.
10 motor cars were stopped and searched, all correct.

（签名）
（签名）

1932年6月8日，星期三。

华籍
电话
雇员
罢工。
1932年6月7日晚上8时20分，接到中央无线电接收站（C.C.R.）的电话消息，称上海电话公司的雇员已罢工。
毕晓普督察（Insp. Bishop）和副巡官克劳登（D.P.S. Crowden）立即前往麦赫斯特路（Modhurst Road，原文拼写错误，应为Medhurst）西区交换局，经查明，五名员工的夜班人员于1932年6月7日晚7时左右毫无预警地离职。罢工原因被认为是为了加薪。
预计20人的白班也将罢工，因为西区交换局经理表示，他们预计明天（1932年6月8日）会发生罢工，因此显然这是一次普遍的行动。后来查明，租界内几乎所有交换局都处于相同状况。
然而，在西区交换局，自动系统由外籍员工操作。已在该交换局部署了一名外籍警长和三名中国巡捕（C.P.C.s）组成的警力守卫，在卢塞恩的法商交换局也部署了类似的守卫，那里的工人目前仍在继续工作。
已通知并出席的是“B”区值班少校温赖特（Major Wainwright）。
调查正在进行中。

巡逻。
1932年6月7日上午11时至下午1时以及晚上7时至8时之间，一辆无线电厢式车在该地区的各条道路上巡逻。

Diary for Information of Commissioner of Police
----
10.50 a.m. 8/6/32
Supt. Robertson

Shanghai Telephone Company - strike of Chinese mechanics

A lightning strike of mechanics in the various
exchanges commenced at 7 p.m. June 7 when the five night
duty mechanics of the Western Exchange quit work and
their action was immediately followed by their colleagues
in the six exchanges of the Company in the International
Settlement and two in The French Concession. Steps
were promptly taken by the Company to meet the situation
with the result that this morning despite the absence of
many of the day mechanics, the entire telephone service is
operating on a normal basis. Following the initial
strike at the Western Exchange, it was found that several
of the lines there had been tampered with but only to
a minor degree and the defects were quickly adjusted.

Due to the fact that to-day is a holiday the
Company is not in a position to state how many of its 400
mechanics are on strike. No demands have been made by
the strikers and it is surmised that their action is to
demonstrate their sympathy for employees, principally
operators who have been dismissed as a result of the
installation of the automatic system. It is not known
that the mechanics had any grievance of their own, as
they were not affected by the introduction of the new
system.

It is learned that since July last the services
of over 2,000 employees have been dispensed with, each
employee so dismissed being granted a retiring gratuity
from a provident fund instituted by the Company when
it was decided to transfer the service to automatic.

（左侧手写批注：7 96）

1932 年 6 月 8 日上午 10:50
罗伯逊警司

上海电话公司 - 中国技工罢工

6 月 7 日晚 7 时，各交换局的技工发起了一场突然罢工，当时西区分局的五名夜班技工停止工作，他们的行动立即得到了该公司在国际租界内六个交换局以及法租界内两个交换局的同事的响应。公司迅速采取措施应对局势，结果是尽管许多白班技工缺席，但今天上午整个电话服务仍正常运行。在西区分局发生初步罢工后，发现那里的几条线路遭到人为破坏，但程度轻微，缺陷已迅速修复。

由于今天是假日，公司无法说明其 400 名技工中有多少人正在罢工。罢工者未提出任何要求，据推测，他们的行动是为了表示对被解雇员工（主要是因安装自动系统而被解雇的话务员）的同情。据悉，技工们自身并无不满，因为新系统的引入并未影响到他们。

获悉，自去年七月以来，已有 2000 多名员工被解雇，每位被解雇的员工都从公司决定转为自动服务时设立的公积金中获得了一笔退休金。

（左侧手写批注：7 96）

Supplementary to the Intelligence Report of 7/8/32

Translation of handbill obtained from the Shanghai Telephone
Company on 7/8/32 :-

MANIFESTO ISSUED BY THE GENERAL REPRESENTATIVE MEETING OF
THE TELEPHONE COMPANY EMPLOYEES AND WORKERS:

Labourers and other people in Shanghai :

The cruel oppression and extortion practised by the
American Imperialists have reduced us to an extremely painful
condition which we can no longer endure. We, for our own
emancipation, should unite together and fight persistently against
the Telephone Capitalists.

While Japan and other Imperialists have been
drastically attacking China since September 18, 1932, the
American capitalists have launched an attack on the telephone
workers. Several hundred workers have been dismissed. A
further 300 whose services were punctual and satisfactory while
the hostilities lasted, will be thrown out of work and replaced
by Russians within the month of June. The annual increase in
wages due in April was not granted this year and the practice of
granting holidays on Sundays has been discontinued. Deposits
made by workers who have been employed in the company for more
than 10 or 20 years, have been seized without substantial reasons.
All this shows clearly that the Imperialistic capitalists are out
to suck the blood of the workers.

In the past various ways and means have been used by
the capitalists and the running dogs who assist them to dissipate
our strength, so that we would not be able to engage in struggle.
The 18 demands submitted by the Union last year were treated
as a scrap of paper. Unless drastic measures are now adopted
towards the capitalists, our interests will suffer severely.
page_data.zh:
对 1932 年 8 月 7 日情报报告的补充

1932 年 8 月 7 日从上海电话公司获得的传单译文：-

电话公司员工和工人代表联席会议发布的宣言：

上海的劳工和其他民众：

美国帝国主义者实施的残酷压迫和勒索使我们陷入了极其痛苦的境地，我们再也无法忍受。为了自身的解放，我们应该团结起来，坚持不懈地与电话资本家作斗争。

自 1932 年 9 月 18 日以来，当日本和其他帝国主义者猛烈攻击中国时，美国资本家也对电话工人发起了攻击。数百名工人被解雇。另有 300 名在敌对行动期间表现准时且令人满意的工人，将在六月份被解雇并由俄罗斯人取代。原定四月发放的年度加薪今年未予批准，周日休假的做法也已取消。在公司工作了 10 或 20 年以上的工人所缴纳的押金，在没有充分理由的情况下被没收。所有这些都清楚地表明，帝国主义资本家意在榨取工人的血汗。

过去，资本家及其帮凶使用各种手段来分散我们的力量，使我们无法进行斗争。工会去年提交的 18 项要求被视作废纸。除非现在对资本家采取严厉措施，否则我们的利益将遭受严重损害。

page_data.en:
In order to realize our demands we swear to use the strike
weapon and to persevere until the end.
We hope that labourers and people of other classes in
Shanghai will give us material or moral support in our
fight against the Imperialistic Capitalists.
Our demands are as follows:-
1. That the dismissal of workers and the practice of increasing
the amount of work to be done by each individual be
opposed.
2. That dismissed workers be reinstated and those who resign
on their own accord be granted, in addition to their
deposits, a retiring gratuity equivalent to 6 months'
wages.
3. That the wages of 'old' and 'new' workers be increased.
(commencing from April ).
4. That double wages be paid to employees who work on holidays.
5. That deposits made by workers be returned to them.
6. That the working hours in the boiler room be made equal
to those in other departments.
7. That full wages be paid to workers during periods when they
are absent on sick leave.
8. That no worker of the Switch Room or Test room be assigned
to do work of a character usually undertaken by coolies.
9. That vacancies which arise be given to former workers of
the Company.
10. That the employing of 'White' Russians be opposed.
11. That the proposal to increase telephone charges be opposed.
page_data.zh:
为了实现我们的要求，我们发誓使用罢工这一武器，并坚持到底。
我们希望上海的劳工和其他阶层人士在我们反对帝国主义资本家的斗争中给予我们物质或道义上的支持。
我们的要求如下：-
1. 反对解雇工人以及增加每个人工作量的做法。
2. 复职被解雇的工人，并对自愿辞职者除退还押金外，另给予相当于六个月工资的退休金。
3. 提高“老”工人和“新”工人的工资（从四月开始）。
4. 向在节假日工作的员工支付双倍工资。
5. 将工人缴纳的押金退还给他们。
6. 锅炉房的工作时间应与其他部门相同。
7. 工人在病假期间应支付全额工资。
8. 不得指派交换室或测试室的工人从事通常由苦力承担的工作。
9. 出现的空缺职位应提供给公司的前员工。
10. 反对雇佣“白”俄罗斯人。
11. 反对提高电话费的提议。

Shanghai Telephone Company - strike of Chinese employees
The situation remains unchanged.
In accordance with the arrangements made by the
Strike Committee, about 200 strikers gathered in the neigh-
bourhood of the Fokien Road Exchange at about 9 a.m. June 10.
At about 10 a.m. four delegates called on the Management of
the Company in the Fokien Road Exchange when the latter
informed them that the Company would have to thoroughly
consider the demands submitted by them on June 9 before a
definite reply could be given. Being dissatisfied with this
declaration, one of the delegates on leaving the premises
shouted the progress of negotiations to the gathering and
urged them to announce their attitude in dealing with the case.
Thereupon the crowd shouted "Strike" "Strike" and appeared to
be excited. With a view to avoiding disorder, the Police
dispersed the crowd and took into custody five persons for
refusing to obey the order to go away. These were subse-
quently released. The crowd however subsequently re-formed
and proceeded in small batches to the Public Recreation
Ground with the object of holding a meeting there, but on
arriving at the latter place at about 11 a.m. they were
prohibited by the Chinese Police from carrying out their
object on the ground that they had not secured permission
from the Social Bureau. The crowd then dispersed after
having arranged to assemble at 2 p.m. the same day at Tsei
Tsung Kuo Teashop, Chekiang and Ningpo Roads corner.

根据罢工委员会的安排，约200名罢工者于6月10日上午9时左右聚集在福建路交换局附近。上午10时左右，四名代表前往福建路交换局面见公司管理层，后者告知他们，公司在给予明确答复之前，必须对他们于6月9日提出的要求进行彻底考量。因对该声明不满，其中一名代表在离开办公场所时，向聚集的人群喊话通报谈判进展，并敦促他们宣布对此案的处理态度。随即人群高呼“罢工”、“罢工”，情绪显得激动。为避免混乱，警方驱散了人群，并以拒不服从离去命令为由拘留了五人。这些人随后被释放。然而，人群之后又重新集结，分批前往公共游乐场，意图在那里举行集会，但当他们在上午11时左右到达该地时，中国警察以未获得社会局许可为由，禁止他们实现这一目的。人群随后散去，并约定于当日下午2时在浙江路与宁波路拐角处的“蔡宗国”茶馆重新集合。

Labour (3) June 11, 1932

The following is translation of a handbill, copies of which
were distributed by the strikers while en route to and from the
Public Recreation Ground, West Gate:

" The 2nd Manifesto issued by the Shanghai Telephone Company
Strikers' Committee.

Peoples of various circles and labourers in Shanghai and
other places in China:

We have issued the 1st Manifesto since the declaration
of the strike by our 3,000 labour comrades at 7 p.m. June 7
and in that manifesto we have explained the object of our
movement. Of course we are struggling for our own welfare;
opposing the dismissal of workers and demanding an increase in
wages, but nevertheless we are fighting for our nation against
the aggression in China by the Imperialists who massacre our
brethren. Consequently if anyone forbids us to join the
strike and declares this movement "illegal", causing a breach
of the Public Peace, he is assisting the Imperialists in
oppressing us; and is therefore a "running dog" of the
Imperialists, a traitor and a spy.

Based on the experience gained from the strike of workers
of local newspaper offices, post offices, etc. we oppose
mediation by anybody. We want direct negotiations with the
Management in connection with our demands. If anyone intends
to break our strike on the pretext of mediation and "sells"
our movement so as to make our efforts useless, he is
assisting the Imperialists in oppressing us and is there-
fore a "running dog" of the Imperialists, a traitor and a
spy. Let all our 3,000 strikers unite together and be
on our guard against any labour traitors or spies who will
not refrain from employing deceitful or forcible measures
and fabricating rumours to counteract our activities. We
hope that all Chinese workers will render full support in order
to make our strike a success which will at the same time mean
a victory in our anti-Imperialistic struggle.

The Shanghai Telephone Company
Strikers' Committee - June 9 "

At 2 p.m. June 10, about thirty strikers appeared at
the Tsai Tsung Kuo Teashop, corner of Chekiang and Ningpo
Roads but owing to the surveillance kept by the Police it
was decided to abandon the meeting.

The Strikers' Communication office is in Room 85 Tung
Saung Hotel, 42 Avenue Road, where information regarding the
strike is issued to the Public.

以下是传单的译文，该传单由罢工者在往返西门公共游乐场途中分发：

“上海电话公司罢工委员会发布的第二号宣言。

上海及中国各地的各界人士和劳工们：

自6月7日晚7时我们三千名劳工同志宣布罢工以来，我们已发布第一号宣言，并在该宣言中阐明了我们运动的目标。当然，我们是为自身的福利而斗争；反对解雇工人并要求增加工资，但与此同时，我们也是在为国家而战，反对那些屠杀我们同胞的帝国主义列强对中国的侵略。因此，如果有人禁止我们参加罢工，并宣称此运动为‘非法’，造成破坏公共和平，他就是在协助帝国主义压迫我们；因此他是帝国主义的‘走狗’、叛徒和间谍。

基于从当地报社、邮局等工人罢工中获得的经验，我们反对任何人的调解。我们要就我们的要求与管理层进行直接谈判。如果任何人企图以调解为借口破坏我们的罢工，并‘出卖’我们的运动，致使我们的努力付诸东流，他就是在协助帝国主义压迫我们，因此他是帝国主义的‘走狗’、叛徒和间谍。让我们三千名罢工者团结起来，警惕那些不择手段使用欺骗或暴力措施以及制造谣言来对抗我们活动的工贼或间谍。我们希望所有中国工人给予全力支持，以使我们的罢工取得成功，这也同时意味着我们反帝斗争的胜利。

上海电话公司
罢工委员会 - 6月9日”

Labour
June 10, 1932.

The Shanghai Telephone Company - Strike of Mechanics

The situation to-day shows little change, although a number
of members of the clerical staff have failed to report for duty.
The Company estimate that there are approximately a thousand
employees on strike to-day.

At about 2.15 p.m. June 9 about 150 strikers congregated out-
side the Fokien Road Exchange (Ningpo Road corner) and four of
their number who had been selected as delegates sought an inter-
view with the Manager of the Exchange. It was pointed out to them
that he was then at the Head Office, Kiangse Road, and consequently
they (the delegates) proceeded there in a motor car. The crowd,
which was quite orderly, dispersed at the request of the Police
but again re-formed and followed the delegates to the Head Office.
At the Head Office, the delegates submitted a petition translation
of which is as follows:-

"We beg to inform you that we are working for the Company
at very meagre wages while the cost of living is very high.
These facts are well known to the Company as well as people in
the Union. On the 28th Jan. the Sino-Japanese conflict broke out
and the people residing in the affected areas escaped to
places of safety but we, the workmen risking our lives, worked
under gunfire as usual.
"Not only did we receive no reward for this but the Company
abolished work on Sunday and also abolished the usual practice of
giving an increase of salary in April and moreover a great number
of workmen were discharged. Our savings are often deducted as
fines. The Company is replacing Chinese employees by White Rus-
sians. We cannot stand this oppressive treatment. Other examples
of unfairness cannot be given in detail in writing. Accordingly
we, the workmen went on strike on June 7th and submitted the
following demands and asked the Company to answer within 18 hours:
1. Both old and new workmen to receive an increase in wages, those
earning less than $20.00 should get an increase of $10.00,
those who get less than $30.00 an increase of $8.00 and less
than $40.00 an increase of $5.00.

（印：SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE C. & S. B. REGISTRY No. D 3728 Date 10 / 6 / 32）

上海电话公司——机务员罢工

今日局势变化不大，尽管部分职员未能报到上班。公司估计今日约有千名员工罢工。

6月9日下午2时15分左右，约150名罢工者聚集在福建路交换局（宁波路拐角）外，其中四名被选为代表的罢工者寻求会见交换局局长。有人向他们指出，局长当时在江西路总公司，于是他们（代表们）乘汽车前往那里。人群秩序井然，应警方要求解散，但随后又重新集结，并跟随代表们前往总公司。在总公司，代表们提交了一份请愿书，译文如下：-

“谨告知阁下，我们在公司为极微薄的工资工作，而生活成本极高。这些事实为公司及工会人士所共知。1月28日，中日冲突爆发，居住在受影响地区的民众逃往安全地带，但我们工人冒着生命危险，照常枪林弹雨下工作。
“我们不仅未因此得到任何奖励，公司反而取消了星期日的工作，并取消了通常在四月加薪的做法，此外还解雇了大量工人。我们的积蓄常被作为罚款扣除。公司正用白俄雇员取代华籍员工。我们无法忍受这种压迫性待遇。其他不公事例无法在书面上一一详述。据此，我们工人于6月7日罢工，并提出以下要求，请公司在18小时内予以答复：
1. 新老工人均须加薪，月薪低于20.00元者加薪10.00元，低于30.00元者加薪8.00元，低于40.00元者加薪5.00元。

（印：上海公共租界工部局警务处 刑事与特别股登记处 编号 D 3728 日期 10 / 6 / 32）

2. We are opposed to the dismissal of workers and those whose
services were dispensed with on May 30 should be reinstated
with full wages to date.

3. Wages of workmen during the period of strike should be paid.

4. The Company should recognize the representatives of the Workmen's
Union. The Company should also provide office accommodation
for the Union and in future all questions between workmen and
capitalists be handled through the Union.

5. Female operators should be given two months for rest before
and after childbirth together with $50.00 medical fees.

6. Employees discharged between February 18 and May 30 should be
given a gratuity from the superannuation fund and pay in lieu
of notice.

"We trust the Company will immediately comply with the above
demands, giving due consideration to the actual conditions of the
workmen.

"The Company is expected to comply with the following demands
so that they may serve as preliminary step for settling controversies
between the workmen and the company:

1. There shall be no increase of working hours on any grounds and
the workmen shall only work 7 hours per day and female employees
6 hours per day.

2. In addition to the increase of wages as provided in one of the
demands further increases shall be made in accordance with the
rise in the price of commodities and house rental.

3. There shall be no work on Sundays, nor on days for meeting of
the workmen's union and other official holidays. We are
opposed to the abolition of the practice of double pay for
work on Sundays and holidays.

4. The superannuation fund and the 6 months wages for retired
employees be given into their custody for safe keeping.

5. Employees receiving injuries or disabled for life in carrying
out their duties shall be given compensation until recovery
or for life as the case may be.

6. In case of death occurring during performance of official duty
the deceased's family be given $5,000 and his children 10
years free education.

7. Those who retire at an age of over 50 be given an old age
pension equivalent to his wages.

8. On leave of absence due to sickness, marriage or funeral wages
should be paid regularly and the Company should give the sick
employees medical fees and after recovery they should be allowed
to return to work. Besides the foreign doctor there shall be
a Chinese doctor.

“我们相信公司会立即遵守上述要求，充分考虑到工人的实际情况。

“期望公司遵守以下要求，以此作为解决工人与公司之间争议的初步步骤：

1. 任何情况下不得增加工作时间，工人每日仅工作7小时，女雇员每日工作6小时。

2. 除其中一项要求规定的加薪外，还应根据物价和房租上涨情况进一步加薪。

3. 星期日、工人工会开会日及其他法定假日不得工作。我们反对取消星期日及节假日双倍工资的做法。

4. 养老金基金及退休员工的六个月工资应交由其保管以确保安全。

5. 在执行职务中受伤或终身残疾的员工，视情况给予补偿直至康复或终身。

6. 如在执行公务期间死亡，给予死者家属5,000元，其子女享受十年免费教育。

7. 年满50岁以上退休者，应给予相当于其工资的养老金。

8. 因病、婚丧请假期间，工资应照常发放，公司应给予患病员工医疗费，康复后应允许其返岗。除外籍医生外，还应配备一名中医。

July 15, 32.

My dear Gill

Some days ago you called to thank the Police Force for the assistance given to the Telephone Company during the strike. At the same time you asked me to give you some indication of the men who made special efforts in the matter.

Superintendent Robertson of the Special Branch supervised the work of the men who specially watched the strike and was on tap day and night throughout. He was largely responsible for any value that may be attached to assistance rendered by the Police.

The other men who contributed towards the effort of the Police were:
Two Chinese detective Sub-Inspectors
Two 1st class clerks
Two 3rd class clerks
Six Chinese detective constables
One Special Branch Agent.

This is, I think, the information you asked for.
I regret the delay in giving you the information due to delay in getting in reports.

Yours sincerely,

(Sd) F. W. Gerrard

F. Gill, Esq.,
Vice President,
Shanghai Telephone Company.

1932年7月15日。

我亲爱的 Gill

特务处（Special Branch）的罗伯逊（Robertson）巡官监督了专门监视罢工的警员的工作，并在此期间日夜待命。警队所提供的协助若有价值，很大程度上归功于他。

其他为警队工作做出贡献的人员包括：
两名华籍侦探副巡官
两名一级文员
两名三级文员
六名华籍侦探巡长
一名特务处线人。

我想这就是你所要求的信息。
因等待报告汇入导致延误，未能及时向你提供信息，深表歉意。

此致

敬礼，

（签名） F. W. Gerrard

上海电话公司。

Subject (in full) Work of the Special Branch in connexion with the strike
of workers of the Shanghai Telephone Company

Made by .................................... and .................................... Forwarded by Supt. Robertson

The work of maintaining contact with the strikers and
securing information regarding their plans was carried out
in an efficient manner by agents and detectives of the
Special Branch. In addition to the translation of handbills
issued by the strikers, the Special Branch drafted three
different manifestoes in Chinese which the Company distributed
amongst the strikers. The drafting of these documents took
considerable time and care and was done at the request of
Mr. Gill, Vice-President and Mr. Porter, General Manager,
to ensure against any attempt on the part of the Company's
clerical staff to misrepresent the Company's position
vis-a-vis the strike. Even after these notices had been
mimeographed at the Company's office distribution was
withheld until a sample copy had been submitted to the
Special Branch and checked with the original draft.
The following members of the Staff were responsible for this
work verbal appreciation of the value of which has been
expressed by both Mr. Gill and Mr. Porter:
D.I. Sih Tse-liang
D.I. Kuh Pao-hua
1st Class Clerk Zung Zoong-oen
1st Class Clerk Kao Yen-keng
3rd Class Clerk Loh Wei-kong

SHANGHAI TELEPHONE COMPANY

June 24, 1932.

J. R. Jones, Esq.,
Secretary,
Shanghai Municipal Council,
209 Kiangse Road.

Dear Sir:

I desire to express on behalf of Shanghai Telephone
Company its indebtedness to the Police Department of the
International Settlement for the very effective protection
given to its various offices and staff during the strike of
about one third of the Company's Chinese workers between
June 7th and 23rd.

Our anxiety regarding the protection of buildings
containing very expensive equipment, was almost entirely
relieved by the very efficient protection obtained. We were
thus enabled to devote our attention to maintaining the service
and getting the personnel back to work again.

I should feel grateful if you would be good enough
to bring this expression of our thanks to the notice of
the Council.

Yours sincerely,
(Signed) F. Gill.
Vice President.

P.O. No. 254.270f. 30/. 6/. 32..

On June 9th, Shanghai Telephone Company received two documents 
purporting to come from a body calling itself Shanghai Telephone 
Company, Workmens! Strike Committee; in one of these documents the 
reasons for the present strike of workers are set out as follows: - 


1. The Company did not reward the conduct of the workmen 
who continyed work during the recent hostilities. 


2. The Company abolished the rule regarding Sunday work 
and April increases. 


3. The Company dismissed a great number of workers not 


only without compensation but has denied them participa- 
tion in the superannuation fund, this fund being con-

Place of Chinese, 
on these grounds it is stated that the workers declared a 
strike at 7 p.em. on the 7th June and it is to be noted that no advance ,,

doned the service of the Public and having ceased work now make 


certain demands.

days on which they could not return to work due to 
the hostilities. . 


b. During the hostilities nearly double the usual 
amount of overtime money was paid to the workers. 


c. Many workers were given food free of cost. 


a. Many workers and their fahiliés were housed by the Company.

pay is due to the progress of the reconstriction 
programme. -
